title: The work list
dek: What is being done here, as opposed to what is known.
lead: Every other register in this archive answers what is **known** — [what has been searched](/searched/), [what is still open](/open-questions/), [what was got wrong](/corrections/). None of them answered **what is being done**, so that lived in a chat window, which is the one place that does not survive the session. Three times in one week someone asked this archive what it was working on, and three times the answer was typed out and then lost. This is that answer, written down. It is deliberately short on findings and long on **who has to move each thing** — an item with no owner is how a list becomes wallpaper.
close:
Written 15 September 2026, in the shape the Defranceschi session settled on, so that eight archives keep one list rather than eight people each inventing one.

**Extended the same day into a roadmap.** The first twenty-two rows were what happened to be in hand. Rows 23 to 48 were built instead from what the archive already knows about itself: `coverage.json` says **34 of the 70 direct ancestors have no document**; `targets.json` ranks every filmed book by how many of them it would reach; `consistency.json` and `impossible.json` hold **116 contradictions** the tree has never been asked to explain. The rows are in yield order, and the yield is measured rather than guessed — **Karlobag deaths reach ten direct ancestors and that book's A–Z index is already mapped to the letter**, which is why it is row 23 and not row 40.

Three of them are not research at all but the conditions for it: **twenty-one ancestors have no place recorded**, so no film can be chosen for them (row 34); **a DGS number does not reliably name a book** (row 42); and **nobody has written down which parish the record index covers**, so every sitting rediscovers whether its next job is an hour or a week (row 43).

**And one gate added the same day, for the failure the list could not see in itself.** `checkworklist.py` checks the rows a list has; nothing checked the rows it was missing, and this list quietly showed **four letters where five had been sent**. `tools/checkcovers.py` now counts it against the register's **pending** rows and the contents of **`requests/sent/`**, and the build refuses when something outstanding has no row — or when a row still points at something retired. It caught **two more gaps** on its first run, and threw out its own first draft for containing an exemption that excused one of them.

rows.what: Rebuild the Žubrinić households of Šumećica by house number — all fifteen read
rows.note:
**All fifteen read, 15 September 2026, and [question 4](/open-questions/) 4d is answered: the Michaels are at least seven men, in seven houses, in four villages.** **Šumećica N° 5** (four children, 1849–58), **Šumećica N° 10**, **Poljica N° 13**, **Prozor N° 50**, **Obilje N° 7** and **Prozor Br. 1** — six distinct wives. The *Conditio* column separates them and nothing else does.

**Šumećica N° 5 is a household this archive did not have** — Michael Žubrinić and Maria Marković, four children across nine years. The Šumećica houses known before were N° 2, N° 10 and N° 24.

**Three Žubrinić women married Žubrinić men**, and the index carries a given name only for every one of them. **The index is also wrong at least once**: it gives the 1852 mother at Šumećica N° 5 as «Maria Maković» where the register says **Marković** — a household that looked like two is one.

The last entry, Maria of 28 November 1858, came in a third window: **Prozor N° 49**, next door to N° 50. Everything is in `sources/familysearch/otocac-michael-1846-1858.json`, and the cautions that cost this sitting time are in [notes/otocac-michael-house-numbers-2026-09-15.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/otocac-michael-house-numbers-2026-09-15.md) — the book **changes language from page to page**, the **status word drifts while the house number holds**, and entries hide in the last row of a left page below where a whole-page crop stops.

**Reconciled against the tree.** The households are not new people: all six wives and nine of the fourteen children are already there. **What the tree lacked was the house numbers** — of those nine children exactly one carried one, *Nikola Miko Žubrinić*, «Prozor 50», which this reading confirms; the rest said «Otočac, Croatia» or nothing. Seven are now in `sources/readings.psv`, and **five children genuinely absent from the tree** are in `sources/found.psv`, every one of them with siblings the tree already has.

**A caution worth more than the finding.** A first check concluded that none of the six wives was in the tree. That was wrong: they appear only as **parent references on their children**, with no page of their own, so a search of published people misses them. **Searching `people.json` is not searching the tree**, and a «not in the tree» claim made that way is worthless.

rows.what: Karlobag folios 6 and 4 — and ahnentafel 54's marriage, found on folio 4
rows.note:
**Found 15 September 2026, where this row expected a null.** Ahnentafel 54 married ahnentafel 55 at Karlobag on **17 June 1807**, folio 4, image 231: «…habito mutuo consensu ***Georgii filij defti Georgii Uroda*** et ***Mariæ filiæ Michaelis Gergas*** hujatium… præsentibus testibus *Caspare Jerko viduo* et *Joanne Fero…*». The date column reads 17 and the month is a ditto for the entry above it, *16 Junii*; the page runs 7 Jan · 14, 22, 26 *ejusdem* · 3 Feb · 7 May · 16 Jun · **17** · 8 Jul · 20 Sep, so the ditto can only be June.

**It proves the two brothers.** The 1806 marriage of *Joannis filii defuncti Dñi Georgij Uroda* was read at the time as probably a brother rather than ahnentafel 54 himself, because ahnentafel 55's 1834 death entry calls her husband a *Georgius*. Confirmed from the other side: **Joannes and Georgius are both sons of the same dead Georgius Uroda**, married sixteen months apart in the same church. Ahnentafel 108 is named here as «defti Georgii Uroda», tying the 1791 burial to both marriages.

**Two cautions.** The volume's own index put a Georgius Uroda on **folio 6** — folio 6 has now been read **end to end, both pages, 1809 and 1810 through to the «Finis», and holds no Uroda at all**. The index's *folium* column does not reliably name the leaf. And the doubt carried as «Martini U[roda?]» in the 18 January 1809 entry reads, at five times full resolution, **Uzelac** — settled, and not a lead. Full record in [notes/karlobag-1807-uroda-gergas.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/karlobag-1807-uroda-gergas.md).

rows.what: Selce deaths — ahnentafel 24 and 25 read, and the cholera that took him
rows.note:
**Ahnentafel 25 is read, 15 September 2026.** LIBER DEFUNCTORUM p. 144, image 397: «**Udova Maria Antić, supruga pok. Josipa, kći Jurja i Mare Jeličić, R. Katolikinja**» — Selce house **29**, aged **73**, died **6 July 1882**, buried the 7th. Widow of ahnentafel 24, daughter of ahnentafel 50, and the age matches a birth of 22 March 1809. The mother is written «Mare» where the tree has ahnentafel 51 as *Margarita* — consistent, not proof, recorded as read.

**The index does not cover this register, which changes how the rest gets done.** A sweep for *Antić* at Selce returns **119 indexed entries and every one is a baptism**. The index-with-ARK shortcut that found the Otočac households and the Karlobag baptism in minutes **does not work here** — this book has to be walked.

**So the film is mapped instead.** 005497948 is 802 images and is not one book: image 200 is a *HISTORIA PAROCHIAE*, the death register runs through the 380s–390s, image 600 is a later Croatian-ruled register, and **the waypoint in the URL changes between images**. Measured: **384 = 1877**, **397 = 1882**, **400 = 1883–84** — about **2.7 images to the year**.

**Ahnentafel 24 is read, 15 September 2026.** Page 99, image 340, ARK `3:1:3QSQ-G99X-13PY`: «*Letta 850. **na 21. 8bre*** · house **74** · **Preminu Osip Antić težak i Mare kćer** · **44 / 6** · ***Od kolere***». **One entry for two people** — Josip and his six-year-old daughter Mare, dead the same day of **cholera**. The age puts his birth in 1805–06 and the tree says 14 March 1806. His house is **74**, not the **29** where his widow died in 1882 — two numbers, thirty-two years and a widowhood apart, recorded as two.

**The page is a casualty list.** *Od kolere* runs down the remarks column; pages 98–99 hold 30 September to 21 October 1850, six deaths on the 10th alone, and **seven other Antić deaths in the eleven days before Josip**. None is claimed.

**A false null was nearly written and the page numbers stopped it** — 99, [100], 101 across images 340 and 341, so the jump from 21 October 1850 to 21 February 1851 is a real gap in the dying, not a lost leaf. Written up in [notes/selce-cholera-1850.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/selce-cholera-1850.md).

**The year map was wrong and is fixed.** Not 2.7 images to the year: **311 = 1834**, **338 = early 1849**, **339–340 = Sept–Oct 1850**, **341 = 1851–52** — about **1.7** through the 1830s–50s, 2.7 only in the 1870s–80s. Arks in `sources/familysearch/film-005497948-selce-deaths.json`.

**What is left is [row 25](/worklist/):** ahnentafel 48 and 49 (1829, ≈ image 302) and 96, 98 and 99 in the 1790s–1800s.

rows.what: Senj marriages 1734–1858 — the marriage of ahnentafel 12 and 13
rows.note:
Their son was baptised **1 November 1857**, so the marriage falls just before it. Their register names are now known exactly — **«Juraj Papa, težak»** and **«Matia rođena Pilipić»** — which is what makes this findable. Not in the index; a film read.

**The FamilySearch block of 15 September 2026 comes and goes — see [row 21](/worklist/).** It shut three times and opened three times in forty minutes, and fifteen register entries were read in those windows. This row is not blocked; it is waiting for the next window, with its targets written down.

---

**20 September 2026 — which books are indexed is now measured rather than assumed.** `sources/familysearch/indexed.psv` holds the table, probed parish by parish through the persona search API. **And the first version of that table was wrong, corrected the same day: marriages and deaths ARE indexed**, through *Hungary, Croatia-Slavonia, Marriages 1678–1927* and *…Deaths 1681–1990*. They were invisible because **the search is ranked and capped** — a broad query returns about sixty rows and whole collections sit below the cut. **Narrow by date and they appear.** **Tested directly for this row and it is not there.** Searches for a Georgius Papa or Papić marriage, for a Matia Pilipić marriage, and for a Papić × Pilipić pair all return nothing. **Row 4 remains what it always said it was: a film read**, and that is now a measured fact rather than an expectation.

**Retested against the marriage index that does exist, and it is still not there.** Five queries — Juraj Papić × Matia, Georgius Papa × Pilipić, Matia Pilipić × Papa, × Papić, and Papić marriages at Senj and at Selce in the 1850s. **Every hit is the 1885 marriage of their SON Josip**, where the two of them appear as his parents. The index holds the son's marriage and not theirs. **Row 4 is a film read**, now tested five ways rather than assumed.

rows.what: Ahnentafel 53's baptism — found: Oliva Maria Smojver, 11 March 1781
rows.note:
**Found 15 September 2026.** «Ego Joës Antonius Frankovich Parochus Loci baptizavi Infantem ***die 11ma*** hujus natam ex ***Vincentio, et Oliva Smoyver, vulgò Vukić***, Conjugibus hujus Civitatis, cui imposui est nomen ***Oliva Maria***» — Karlobag, page 65, ark `3:1:3QS7-L99C-L998-5`. The month column reads *Ejusdem* under *Martij*, and the next opening begins at 19 March, so **11 March 1781**. The tree had only «MAR 1781».

**It confirms ahnentafel 106 and 107 from the register side** — Vicentius Smojver Vukić and Oliva Bacchi were in the tree but had never been put on a page; one line now names the couple and the child together.

**And it gives a by-name in a parish that had none.** «Smoyver, ***vulgò*** Vukić» — this archive's by-name file was built out of Selce, where the connectors are *aliter · dictus · dicti* and the scribe **underlines** the pair. Karlobag uses ***vulgò*** and does **not** underline. It also explains a name the tree carries without comment: ahnentafel 106 is recorded as «Vicentius Fabiano Smojver **Vukić**» as though Vukić were part of the surname. It is the household name, and the clerk said so.

**A film note this corrects.** `holdings.psv` gives DGS 5481648 as the 1691–1804 baptisms and [notes/karlobag-films.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/karlobag-films.md) calls it a **327-image** film with «image 220 = Anno Domini 1782». Film 005481648 actually has **596 images** and its image 216 is headed **«Godine 1845»**. The 1771–1804 baptisms are under a different waypoint, and the way in was the **record index**, not the film number. Full record in [notes/karlobag-1781-oliva-smojver.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/karlobag-1781-oliva-smojver.md).

rows.note:
**Bribir** 1678 onward — its own parish, filed here as a village of Grižane until the catalogue was read properly. **Sv. Juraj kod Senja** 1697–1852, not in the parish table at all. The **Karlobag *Stanje duša*** beyond the U section. The **Grižane *Popis duša* of 1738**, a household census a century older than Otočac's. All four are in [holdings.psv](/searched/) with their film numbers.

**The FamilySearch block of 15 September 2026 comes and goes — see [row 21](/worklist/).** It shut three times and opened three times in forty minutes, and fifteen register entries were read in those windows. This row is not blocked; it is waiting for the next window, with its targets written down.

---

**21 September 2026 — two of the four are settled without a film being opened, and the honest headline is that three of them reach nobody.**

**The parish-table half of this row is already done.** Bribir and Sv. Juraj (kod Senja) were both added to `parishes.psv` on 14 September, catalogue-verified. What was left was opening the books.

**Two no longer need opening in the way this row imagined.**

* **GRIŽANE IS DENSELY INDEXED**, and `indexed.psv` was badly wrong about it — it said «one hit; treat as untested, not as coverage». A place-only census returns **200 of 200 in both windows, events 1698 to 1894**, and **burials as well as baptisms**: 104 burials against 96 baptisms in the 1800–1899 window. Two collections, including *Croatia, Primorje-Gorski Kotar, Births, from 1569 to 1901*. **The Popis duša of 1738 is still a film read** — a household census is not an event index — but everything around it is a search box.
* **SV. JURAJ KOD SENJA IS A MEASURED ZERO.** Probed place-only under all three strings the parish table gives it — *Sveti Juraj*, *Jurjevo*, *Lukovo* — across 1690–1869. **Nothing.** Filmed 1697–1852 and not indexed, so that one is a sitting or it is nothing.

**AND THE THING THIS ROW SHOULD SAY OUT LOUD: this archive has no person at Bribir, Grižane or Sv. Juraj.** Not one, in any of `bornPlace`, `diedPlace` or `baptisedPlace`. Three of the four books are **breadth**, not descent — worth opening one day, and **not ahead of a book that reaches somebody**.

**The fourth is different.** The **Karlobag *Stanje duša* beyond the U section** is at a parish where this archive has ancestors on the direct line, and no index substitutes for a household census. **That is the one of the four worth a window**, and this row should be read as one target rather than four.

rows.what: Reconcile the stale «pending» rows in the searched register
rows.note:
**Done 15 September 2026.** Three rows were retired, not edited: **Ancestry**, **FamilySearch — Rijeka registers** and **FamilySearch — Otočac, Stanje duša** were *placeholders* — «never», «not yet», «still unread» — and each had been superseded by a real row recording the actual reading. The register was **over-reporting what is outstanding**: eleven pending, of which three were already done. Seven now, and every one of them genuinely open.

**The gate that stops it recurring.** Every register row now declares a `key` — the body of material it covers — and `tools/searched.py` **refuses** when a row is *pending* while any other row with the same key carries a real outcome. The key is there because the source *name* cannot do this job: «Senj marriages, 1734–1858» is genuinely unopened while «Senj marriages, 1859–1920» is read end to end, and a gate matching on names would have called the first one stale and sent a sitting to re-read a book that was already finished. A gate that cries wolf is worse than no gate.

The same stale claim had spread into prose: `/searched` still named **four portals «never once searched»** when all four had been opened, and `requests/README.md` and `REPLIES.md` still said the three letters were **not yet sent** when they went on the 15th. All corrected.

rows.what: Decide where ahnentafel 108 and 109 live
rows.note: **Georgius Uroda** and his wife **Maria** were read out of a register this week and are real. The tree stops at ahnentafel 54 and this archive does not edit the tree — that separation is what the whole project rests on. They are recorded in `sources/found.psv` with ten others, but **nothing on the site shows them** yet. Whether a found person should appear beside the tree, and how, is a decision about what this archive *is*, not a task.

rows.what: Državni arhiv u Rijeci — answered, and it is a refusal
rows.note:
**Answered 15 September 2026, the same day it was sent.** Boris Zakošek: «**Državni arhiv u Rijeci ne provodi ovako složena rodoslovna istraživanja.** Istraživati možete sami u čitaonici Arhiva ili putem internetske stranice familysearch.org» — *the archive does not carry out genealogical research of this complexity; research it yourself in the reading room or on FamilySearch.*

**It refuses the service without answering about the holdings.** The letter asked one question needing no research: whether they **hold, or know who holds, the Rijeka baptismal register covering 1 March 1892**. That is unanswered, and it matters — the 1892–99 volume is missing from the film and from its Kazalo both, which is why Ljubomir Blažević's baptism has never been placed.

**The reply points back at FamilySearch**, which the letter had already said — quoting the volume list — has been read to the end with a gap exactly there.

**What is left is the reading room**, which is genuinely offered: this is material that can be consulted in person at Rijeka, by David or by a paid local researcher. That is now the only stated route to the 1892 entry, and it is a decision rather than a task.

rows.what: The alphabet nodes are probably not only a Žubrinić problem
rows.note:
Fifteen nodes named with a single capital letter — **«M Žubrinić Xubrinich Zubrinic»** — were being published as parents of 75 real people and as one another's siblings. A card index typed in as a family. Both the bucket detector and the site's junk filter now refuse them, **but all seven archives share one GEDCOM**, and nothing here has checked whether the same drawers exist under Blažević, Papić, Prpić or Kalanj. **The test is four lines** and belongs in the kit rather than in this archive.

---

**21 September 2026 — answered, and the answer is two answers pointing opposite ways.**

**THE PROBLEM IS UNIQUE TO ŽUBRINIĆ.** A sibling set of three or more in which *every* member is alphabet-shaped and dateless fires **once in all 15,643 records**: family `@F501632@`, the fifteen, with **eighty-two real people published as their children**. Every other sibling set holding an alphabet-shaped member has **one or two of them among real siblings** — Corbett 2 of 11, De Franceschi 1 of 14, Jelcic 1 of 11, Defranceschi 1 of 10, Willemse 1 of 6, Leonesio 2 of 5, D'Arcy 1 of 3.

**THE TEST IS NOT UNIQUE TO ŽUBRINIĆ, AND THAT IS THE WARNING.** This row says «the test is four lines and belongs in the kit». **The four-line version has ten real people in its blast radius.** The per-node test — one leading capital, a surname, no dates — matches **31 records**, and only fifteen are the drawer. The other sixteen are in the sister archives:

    W Florance Barry · H E Corbett · J C Corbett · J M Willemse · G Norman D'Arcy
    H W Pretorius · N L S Klaassen · E Riedo Defranceschi · J B D Defranceschi · M K Defranceschi

**These are people recorded by their initials**, which is an ordinary English and Afrikaans convention and not a filing artifact. *H E Corbett* is a man his own family knew by his initials. The remaining six are lone letters with **no children at all** — stubs that parent nobody and misfile nothing.

**SO THE RULE IS ABOUT A SET, NOT A NODE.** What makes the fifteen a drawer is not that each is a letter; it is that **they are entered as one another's siblings** and eighty-two people hang off them. A single initial tells you nothing. **A family all of whose children are single initials is a filing cabinet.**

**Nothing changed here, deliberately** — `buckets.py` and the junk filter already refuse the fifteen, and the other sixteen are outside this archive's surname scope. The measurement and the warning have gone to the session that keeps the kit, which is where this row said the test belongs. [notes/the-alphabet-is-one-drawer-the-test-is-not.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/the-alphabet-is-one-drawer-the-test-is-not.md)

rows.what: Six methods found here that the other archives will need
rows.note:
**The index gives the image.** FamilySearch's record search returns the **image ARK** of every indexed entry, so a record opens at the page in one step instead of being hunted down a film — that single fact produced most of this week's findings. **A third FamilySearch failure state**: a sign-out takes *everything* (503, redirect to the sign-in host) where a rate-limit blip and a session block leave the catalogue answering — written into `tools/familysearch.md`. **And `sources/found.psv`**, somewhere to put people read out of a register whom the tree does not have; every archive here will hit that wall.

**Fourth — the register cannot be trusted to retire its own rows.** `/searched` here said eleven sources were outstanding when three had been read and closed: each was a «not yet» placeholder left standing because the reading went into a *new* row. Over-reporting what is outstanding is the same lie as under-reporting it, and it costs a sitting that re-opens a finished book. The fix generalises: **every row declares a `key` naming the body of material it covers, and the checker refuses a *pending* row when another row with that key has a real outcome.** The key is the whole trick — matching on the source *name* would flag «Senj marriages, 1734–1858», which is genuinely unopened, against «Senj marriages, 1859–1920», which is read end to end. Every archive that keeps a search register has this bug waiting in it. In `tools/searched.py` here.

**Fifth — there is a fourth FamilySearch failure state, and it is the worst one.** Beside the rate-limit blip, the session block and the sign-out, there is **Error 15**: a 403 «Access Denied» interstitial on *every* path, laid on the egress address rather than the session. Signing in again does nothing. **The diagnostic that tells it apart in one call** is to fetch a Deep Zoom `image.xml` for an ark that read successfully before: a blip or a session block leaves the tile edge answering, and Error 15 takes the tiles down too. If the tiles are gone there is no route to a page and the only moves are to wait or to read from a different network.

**Sixth — a work list cannot see its own omissions, and needs a second list to count against.** The kit's `checkworklist.py` gates the rows a list *has*. Nothing gated the rows it was *missing*, and on 15 September this archive had **five letters sent and four rows** — the missing one being the reply that named three further doors, and therefore the reason three of the other rows existed. **Every row present looked fine in isolation. The list was only wrong in what it did not say.**

`tools/checkcovers.py` here counts the work list against two lists that are already exact: every **`pending` row in the search register** (which means, in the register's own words, «known, wanted, and not yet got») and every letter in **`requests/sent/`**. A row declares what it accounts for in a `covers` field, and the build refuses when something outstanding has no row — **or when a row points at something that no longer exists**, which is how a list goes stale rather than short.

**It found two real gaps on its first run** — Brinje, pending since the 14th with no row, and ahnentafel 11 — and it **rejected its own first draft**: that draft exempted keys beginning `plan/` as «not really work», and the one row so excused turned out to name two baptisms sitting in a book already open. The exemption was noise-reduction dressed as a rule, and there is none now.

**Every archive in the estate keeps a work list and a search register**, so every one of them can be short in exactly this way, and none of them can currently tell.

---

**Sixth and seventh, found 20 September 2026, and they are the two that will travel furthest — because they are both about the SAME mistake: trusting the query you sent instead of the answer you got back.**

**SIXTH — A SURNAME IS THE WORST THING TO SEARCH AN INDEX BY, and every archive here searches by surname first.** Ahnentafel 52's baptism sat in the FamilySearch index for three sittings under **«Piberich»** — a form that occurs **exactly once in the whole parish**, because it is one clerk's reading of one hand rather than a name anybody bore. Six spellings had been tried. No list of guesses ever contains «Piberich».

**The fix is to stop naming the surname.** `q.givenName` + `q.fatherGivenName` + `q.motherGivenName` + a date window + the parish returns the household **whatever the clerk did to the family name** — the given names are short, common and survive a bad hand, and two parents plus a date is already a near-unique key. It returned ahnentafel 52 and three brothers in **one query**. Every archive with a parish register and a mangled surname has this waiting in it.

**SEVENTH — A ZERO IS ONLY EVER «NOT FOUND BY THIS INSTRUMENT», AND A COVERAGE TABLE BUILT FROM ONE INSTRUMENT IS A LIST OF ITS BLIND SPOTS.** `sources/familysearch/indexed.psv` recorded seven parishes as **NOTHING**, each «tested under» two surnames. Re-probed by **place alone, naming no surname**, three of the seven were wrong — Bribir had 80+ indexed deaths, Selce five baptisms, Ledenice four entries. **The Selce row indicted its own method**: it recorded a zero «under Antić» and one of the entries it missed is «Margaritam **Antich**».

**Run the controls.** Karlobag and Senj return 100 of 100 in every window, which is what says the instrument works at all. **And read the place string BACK** — «Bribir» is two villages 200km apart and the wrong one outranks ours 593 to 7; «Smokvica» returned a village in **Slovenia**. **Neither probe is authoritative alone**: the place-only probe returned zero for Krmpote, where the surname probe had found a 1895 baptism the same day. [notes/the-zeros-were-not-all-zeros.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/the-zeros-were-not-all-zeros.md), [notes/karlobag-the-index-calls-them-piberich.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/karlobag-the-index-calls-them-piberich.md)

---

**Eighth, 20 September 2026 — TWO PATHS TO «READ» AND ONLY ONE OF THEM CHECKED.** `readings.psv` here had ninety-three rows and **eight of them credited nobody**: the slug existed in no data file, so `coverage.py` looked it up, got nothing and moved on, and `datecheck.py` did `people.get(slug)`, got `None`, and skipped the row. Nothing crashed and the file looked fuller than it was.

**All four bad slugs were a nickname the slug generator drops and a hand-written row keeps** — `…-MATIJA-pilipic`, `…-VICKO-pilipic`, `…-JOSO-papic`, `…-JURE-antic` — and **all four are direct-line ancestors**. It went unnoticed because those people were *also* graded read through a citation keyed on the GEDCOM id, so the broken path was masked by the working one.

**Any archive that joins hand-written evidence to a generated tree has this.** The fix is four lines: refuse the build on a row whose key names nobody, and print the nearest real key, because the cause is always a near-miss. In `tools/datecheck.py` here.

---

**Ninth, 20 September 2026 — CHECK THAT THE SITE'S EVIDENCE IS IN THE FILES THE TOOLS READ, because here it was not.**

A request to «make sure everything researched is on the site» found the traffic running the other way, and harder. A note written that morning concluded ahnentafel 3's birth date could not be settled because «there is no image yet» — **and the page had been read years before and was published on this site**, image and all, with the entry transcribed. Her 1907 marriage repeats the date in a second hand. **The note had checked the index against the TREE and never against THIS ARCHIVE.**

**Holding `corrections.json` against `readings.psv` found thirteen more**, including **the marriage of 8 December 1920** — the document the whole archive was built around, with its own page on the site — where **ahnentafel 2 and 4 had no readings of any kind.** Fourteen rows recovered; `readings.psv` 93 → 111 rows, dates checkable against the tree 19 → 24, all still agreeing.

**Why it went unseen is the transferable part.** `coverage.py` grades a person read from **either** a reading row **or** a citation keyed on the GEDCOM id. The corrections carried the citation, so everyone graded correctly while the archive's own record of its work quietly did not hold them. **Two paths to a conclusion, and a working one masking a broken one** — the same shape as the eight orphaned slugs found the same day, and the third instance in one sitting.

**`tools/publishedcheck.py`**, a report and not a gate: a correction can legitimately have no reading when what it found is a **disproof** — ahnentafel 20's says «the 1845 baptism is *not* his», and recording that as a reading would assert the opposite. The tool separates disproofs out. [notes/the-evidence-file-under-reported-the-archive.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/the-evidence-file-under-reported-the-archive.md)

**And the one thing genuinely missing from the site has been published.** `sources/familysearch/indexed.psv` — the table that decides how every register row is planned — was read by no tool and shown on no page. It is now at `/indexed/`, built by `tools/indexcoverage.py`, leading with the two occasions it was wrong.

rows.what: Working when the route out is narrow — FamilySearch's block, and the hidden pane
rows.note:
**Error 15, and it comes and goes.** On 15 September 2026 every request to `familysearch.org` began returning **403 «Access Denied — Error 15»** as a full interstitial. It shut at 04:21, opened at 04:30, shut at 04:45, opened at 04:47, shut at 04:51 and opened again at 05:00. **Fifteen register entries were read in those windows**, which is the whole of work list row 1.

**So the lesson is not «wait for it to clear».** It is to have the targets — ARKs, dates, parents — written to disk *before* a window opens, so a ten-minute opening is ten minutes of reading rather than ten minutes of searching. That is what `sources/familysearch/otocac-michael-1846-1858.json` is, and it is why row 1 closed on a day when the site was mostly shut.

**The one-call diagnostic.** Fetch a Deep Zoom `image.xml` for an ARK that read successfully before: a rate-limit blip or a session block leaves the tile edge answering, and Error 15 takes the tiles down too. If `image.xml` returns HTML instead of `<?xml`, there is no route to a page — not the index, not the catalogue, not the scans. Signing in again does nothing; the block is on the egress address, not the session.

**Client IP 168.140.255.212.** Reading from David's own browser on his own network would not be behind this address at all.

---

**A second constraint, and it is the binding one. 15 September 2026: the Browser pane is hidden in the app, and a hidden pane cannot take a screenshot.** Every read of a register scan in this archive goes through one — crop, enlarge, look. Without it, three routes were tried and all three failed:

* **Post the image to a local server.** The page cannot reach `127.0.0.1` at all: the in-app browser applies the private-network rule and an `https` page on familysearch.org gets «Failed to fetch», with no CSP report, for both `127.0.0.1` and `localhost`.
* **Fetch the Deep Zoom tiles from the shell.** `image.dzi` answers **403** with a bot interstitial and the tile path answers **401**. The tiles want the session, and the session is not something this archive will copy out of a browser.
* **Carry the image out as base64 through a tool result.** This *works at small sizes* — a whole page at contact-sheet scale is about 3 KB and arrived intact. It **fails at useful sizes**. A 19,891-byte contact sheet came back with **exactly the right byte count and the wrong SHA-256**: characters substituted, not dropped, silently. Chunking to 76-character lines did not help.

**So there is a ceiling of a few kilobytes, and a register entry at full resolution is above it.** That matters more than it sounds: this archive's own standing rule is that **no date, name or house number is recorded from a page-scale view**, and it exists because a *19* reads as *1* and a flat-topped *2* reads as *7*. Reading through a channel that can alter bytes without saying so would break that rule in a way nothing downstream could catch.

**Text is not affected and was used hard.** The catalogue is JSON, so [row 42](/worklist/)'s eighty-six film notes came out whole and were **verified by SHA-256 against a second fetch** before being written down. That is the shape of the workaround: **anything that can be checksummed can come out; a photograph cannot.**

**Showing the Browser pane again puts rows 4, 6, 7, 24–35 and 54 back within reach.**

---

**20 September 2026 — and the three states can be told apart in one call.**

The notes above describe each failure separately and each test costs a page load. There is a cheaper one: **fetch a catalogue item and read the status code, nothing else.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **200** | signed in and working — the body is JSON with the film notes |
| **401** | **signed out. Stop.** The account holder must sign in. Waiting does not fix an expired session, and credentials are never this archive's to type |
| **403** | **blocked** — the body carries *«Access Denied … Error 15»*. This one **comes and goes**: on 15 September it shut and opened six times in forty minutes and fifteen register entries were read in the open windows |

**The status code alone separates them, and the distinction is the whole decision** — a 403 means wait a few minutes and try again, a 401 means stop and ask. Telling them apart by loading pages costs a minute each time.

**One refinement to what was written on the 15th.** That sign-out gave **503** on the personas endpoint; this one gave **401** on the catalogue endpoint. So the *code varies by endpoint* and is not by itself the signature. **What is invariant is that a signed-out session fails on the catalogue too** — and the catalogue is the cheapest thing to ask.

**Tested today, and the answer was 401.** FamilySearch has been signed out since at least 17 September. It blocks work list rows **4, 6, 7, 24, 25, 26, 27, 29, 31, 32, 33, 35, 50, 51 and 54** — every register row this archive owns. Everything that does not need it carried on: rows 46 and 57 both moved today.
