rows.what: Karlobag deaths 1774–1804 — all four ancestors read, and a widow the index hides
rows.note:
**Corrected 15 September 2026 before it was begun: this is a walk, not a lookup.** The row was written asserting the Karlobag deaths could be reached through the FamilySearch index. They cannot — row 43 tested four surnames and **every Karlobag hit is a baptism**; the 1717–1861 range that suggested otherwise is baptisms throughout.

**The highest-yield target in the archive, and it is already mapped.** `targets.json` says the Karlobag death books reach **ten direct ancestors** — ahnentafel 52, 55, 104, 105, 107, 108, 110, 111, 212 and 220 — more than any other book here. Four of them have **exact death dates inside the 1774–1804 volume**: ahn 212 Josiph Smojver Vukić **16 May 1776**, ahn 104 Jacob Pilipić **10 April 1778**, ahn 220 Nicolaus Gerkacs **30 October 1783**, ahn 105 Catherina Luckinić **29 May 1790**. Ahn 108's burial of 10 September 1791 is already read out of this same book.

**And it needs no walking.** `holdings.psv` records the register at images **356–409** and its **KAZALO A–Z at 410–434, with the letter positions measured** — P.R at 428, R.S 429, S.T 430, T.U 431, U.V 432, V.X 433. Look up *Pilipić*, *Smojver*, *Gerkacs* and *Luckinić* in the index, take the folium, convert with the known folio map (left pages EVEN, folio 62 = image 388), and read four ancestors in an afternoon.

**What the index page actually looks like, now it has been opened.** Image 428 is **P on the left page and R on the right** — the big letter is written at the top centre of each *page*, three column-groups to a page, each *Cognomen · Nomen · dies · folium*. **The entries are ordered by folio, not alphabetically within the letter**: folios 104, 104, 105, 105, 105, 106, 106, reading Perpich · Perpich · Perpich · Perpich · Potocgniak · **Pekkas** · Potocgniak. So a surname is found by scanning the letter's pages, not by jumping to it. Folio converts to image as **image = 388 + (folio − 62) ÷ 2**, left pages even.

**A find already, from the one index page opened:** *«Pekkas Magdalena, 5 Augusti, folio 106»*. **Pekass is three of the direct ancestors with no document** — ahn 213, 426 and 427 — and this is the first time the surname has appeared in a register here at all.

---

**Begun and half done, 15 September 2026. The KAZALO works.**

**Ahnentafel 104 is read** — folio **17**, image **364**, ARK `3:1:3QS7-L99C-GSBG`:

> «**10: Aprilis** · **D. Jacobus Pilepich Capitaneus portûs**, munitus omnibus Sacramentis per M.R. D. Andream Pintor Capellanum Loci, **spiritum Deo reddidit**, … **in propria Crypta in Parochiali Ecclesia existente**, per me Joannem … tumulatus est»

**Three marks of standing in one entry, and this archive had none of them.** ***Capitaneus portûs*** — **captain of the port**, a crown office in a Military Frontier harbour. The ***D.*** is *Dominus*, withheld from the *Decurio* and the *infans* on the same opening. And he is **not in the parish cemetery**: he is in **his own crypt inside the church**. No age is given. [The note](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/karlobag-1778-jacobus-pilepich.md).

**The route, for the three still to do.** Image **427**, right page, is the letter **P** — three dense columns, ordered **by folio**, not alphabetically. «*Pillepich Jacobus · 10 Aprilis · **folio 17***» sits in the third. Then **folio → image**, measured directly: image 364 = folios **16|17**, image 365 = **18|19**, so `image = 356 + folio ÷ 2`. **That disagrees with `holdings.psv` by one** — it puts folio 62 at **387** where the file says **388**. **Read the folio number printed at the top of the page**, every time.

**Ahnentafel 212 is read too — folio 11, image 361, ARK `3:1:3QS7-L99C-G3WG`:** «*16 ejusdem [Maij 1776] · **Josephus Smojver dictus Vukcich, annorum 45**, munitus omnibus [Sacramentis] … in Domino obijt, atque die 17 … in Coemeterio Parochiali tumulatus*». **The tree's date to the day**, and *annorum 45* agrees with its 1731.

**He is not under S. He is under V** — «***Vukich — vide Smojver — 16: Maij — folio 11***». **This KAZALO indexes the household by-name as a headword** and cross-references it to the surname, and does the same on the same page for «*Verbanovich … **vide Urbanovich***». **A surname missing from its own letter is not absent from the book.** For a family already known here as «*Smoyver **vulgò** Vukić*» (1781), that is the difference between an ancestor and a null — and the 1776 entry uses a different connector, ***dictus***.

**Ahnentafel 220 is read** — folio **39**, the right-hand page of image **376**, ARK `3:1:3QS7-L99C-GSBH`: «*30 8bris · **Nicolaus Gergacs annorum 66**, munitus omnibus sacramentis obiit … **in domo filij sui Antonij**, et **die 31: ejusdem** … sepultus est in Cœmeterio … Laterali ex parte dextra Ecclesiæ Parochialis hujus*». **The tree's date to the day**, *annorum 66* agreeing with its 1717 — and **he died in his son Antonius's house**, a Gergacs this archive has never published.

**Two things the sitting taught.**

* **The KAZALO's date can be the burial.** It says «*3i 8bris*»; the register says died the **30th**, buried «*die 31: ejusdem*». That is exactly what [Find a Grave](/port-pirie/) does — a cemetery records the interment, a parish the death — and **a parish index does it too**. Use the index date to *find* an entry, never to record one.
* **The folio arithmetic drifts; the index does not.** Interpolating from folio 17 put folio 39 on image 375, one leaf early, on a page that ends at 18 June 1783. The printed number settled it in one crop. **Interpolate, then read the number at the top of the page.**

**Letter positions measured: G** 418 right (419 left is G and empty), **P** 427–428, **R** 428, **S** 429, **T** 430, **V** 432.

**Ahnentafel 105 is read, and she closes the row** — folio **63**, image **388**, ARK `3:1:3QS7-L99C-G3QY`: «*29 ejusdem [Maij 1790] · **Catharina annorum 70, vidua defti Jacobi [P]ilepich**, obiit in Domino munita omnibus sacramentis, atque **die 30** sepulta est*». **The tree's date to the day** — and what identifies her is her husband's name, not her own: she is the widow of **ahnentafel 104**, the port captain, dead twelve years before her. **The age disagrees**: 70 in May 1790 puts her birth about **1720** where the tree says **30 March 1727**. Recorded, not resolved.

**She is not in the KAZALO's L, and the whole of L was read to prove it** — folios **1–73** and **76–102**, group 3 blank, image 423's L page empty. Five Luckinić entries, none Catharina. **A widow is indexed under her husband's surname**, which is the third time today this archive has met that rule: «*Vukich vide Smojver*», the Senj stones carving a married woman under her husband's name, and now the KAZALO. Two more by-name headwords fell out of the search — «*Ljubicich **dictus** Luxich ut ibi*» and «*Locatelli, **vulgò** Zessich*».

**Year map for this volume**, measured: folio 17 = 1778 · 39 = 1783 · **63 = 1790** · 74 = 1793 — about **3.5 folios to the year**. From image 376 to 394 it is exactly two folios per image; between 364 and 376 it is not.

**All four ancestors in this book are read.** The next one is [row 24](/worklist/), the *Umrli 1804–1861* on the same film, whose own alphabetical index a previous sitting already found at images ~168–192.

**And the index has put Pekass on the table.** Five entries — *Pekas Anton* folio 1, *Blasius* folio 2, *Maria* folio 5, *Joanna* folio 10, *Pekkas Magdalena* folio 106. **Pekass is ahnentafel 213, 426 and 427**, three direct ancestors with no document at all, and the surname had never appeared in a Karlobag register here. **These are index lines, not readings** — no page has been opened.

rows.what: Karlobag deaths 1804–1861 — the later half of the same ten
rows.note:
The other half of row 23's ten. Ahnentafel **52** (Josephus Pilipić, d. 26 June 1828), **55** (Maria Gerkacs, d. 6 August 1834 — the entry already quoted here as «uxor piscatoris Georgii Uroda», but never read out in full), and **111** (Lucia Tomljanović, d. 19 September 1809) all fall in the 1804–1861 volume, which has **its own index** on the same film. Do it after row 23, with the index technique already proved.

---

**20 September 2026 — which books are indexed is now measured rather than assumed.** `sources/familysearch/indexed.psv` holds the table, probed parish by parish through the persona search API. **And the first version of that table was wrong, corrected the same day: marriages and deaths ARE indexed**, through *Hungary, Croatia-Slavonia, Marriages 1678–1927* and *…Deaths 1681–1990*. They were invisible because **the search is ranked and capped** — a broad query returns about sixty rows and whole collections sit below the cut. **Narrow by date and they appear.** **Karlobag deaths are not indexed.** The baptisms are — two collections, 1733–1803 and 1805–1858 — and the deaths are not, under any collection. **Ahnentafel 52, 55 and 111 are a film read**, exactly as this row planned, and the volume's own KAZALO is still the instrument. A search for Lucia Tomljanović at Karlobag returns Smiljan and Krivi Put baptisms and nothing from the death book.

**And the coverage table was then crossed against the people who still need a document — with a flat answer.**

**Not one of the 24 direct ancestors still without a document is reachable by the baptism index.** Every one is either in a parish with no baptism index at all (**Selce, Krmpote, Smokvica, Montani Stanište**), or born before the index's coverage begins (**Vitus Sekula, 1787, against an Otočac index that starts at 1839**), or has **no year and no parish** — which is seventeen of the twenty-four, and is [row 34](/worklist/)'s population.

**That is why this archive stalled on exactly these people**, and it is worth stating plainly: the index was decisive for row 54's Karlobag walls because **Karlobag's is the only index that reaches back to 1733**. Nowhere else does it reach the eighteenth century at all.

**One live thread came out of the crossing.** Ahnentafel **210 Vicentius Luckinić** and **211 Maria** had no place, no date and no document. Their daughter is the anchor: **ahnentafel 105, Catta Luckinić, was born 30 March 1727 at Karlobag** to Vicentius and Maria, which places the household out of the tree alone. **The index adds two children** — **Mikola, 9 December 1719** and **Mare, 13 April 1725**, both entered as *«Vicka Luckinicha»* — eight years and two years before Catta, same rare surname, same parish, same father's given name.

**They are in `found.psv` as candidate siblings and not as proof.** Both entries **name no mother**, so nothing in them distinguishes one Vicko from another. **And Catta's own 1727 baptism is not in the index**: the entire Luckinić holding at Karlobag is **seven entries**, which is the best single measure of how partial this indexing is.

---

**20 September 2026 — and the last Karlobag households came out, with one that looked like a contradiction and was not.**

The parents-query on **ahnentafel 54 × 55** returned four children across three years:

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| 15 February 1810 | Margaritha Maria Uroda | «**JOANNE** Uroda × Maria» |
| **23 April 1810** | **Mathiam Georgiam Uroda** | «**GEORGIO** Uroda × Maria» |
| 25 August 1811 | Joannem Bartholomæum | «**JOANNE** Uroda × Maria» |
| 24 August 1812 | Dominicum Bartholomæum | «**GEORGIO** Uroda × Maria» |

**23 April 1810 is ahnentafel 27**, so the February child cannot be her mother's — nine weeks is not a pregnancy — and for an hour this looked like the index contradicting the tree about ahnentafel 54's own name.

**It is two brothers, and this archive already held the fact that separates them.** Ahnentafel 54 was baptised ***«Joannis Georgij»*** — two given names — and is named alive in 1834 as ***«piscatoris GEORGII Uroda»***: he went by **Georgius**, and married Maria Gerkacs in 1807. **His brother, baptised Joannis in 1784, is already in `found.psv`** with the note *«married Maria filia Nicolai Barletich 10 Feb 1806»*. **Two Uroda brothers, married thirteen months apart, both to women called Maria, both fathering at Karlobag in 1810** — and the only thing telling them apart in the index is which of his two given names the priest used.

**Dominicus Bartholomæus 1812 is ahnentafel 27's brother; Margaritha 1810 and Joannes 1811 are her cousins.** All three in `found.psv`, each saying which household and why.

**And the by-name reached a third generation.** Ahnentafel 212's death entry reads *«Josephus Smojver **dictus VUKCICH**»*, so the index's *«Josepho Vukich × Antonia»* is him: **Heva, 10 April 1766** and **Joanna, 16 May 1770**, two more candidate daughters of ahnentafel 212 × 213. **Ahnentafel 212, 106 and their children are all filed under Vukić as often as under Smojver** — and none of them would have been found by querying the surname alone.

---

**20 September 2026 — the Otočac figure in this row is wrong, and the correction widens the window by nine years.** This row rules ahnentafel 84 out as «Vitus Sekula, 1787, against an Otočac index that starts at **1839**». Measured by place-only census rather than by surname, **the Otočac index begins in 1830**:

| births | indexed entries |
|---|---|
| 1700–1799 | **0** |
| 1800–1829 | 1 (a stray at Dabar, 1816) |
| 1830–1834 | **83** |
| 1835–1837 | **200** |

**The verdict on ahnentafel 84 stands** — 1787 is nowhere near 1830, and there is nothing at Otočac before 1800 under any instrument. **What changes is the boundary**, and `indexed.psv` now carries the measurement instead of the estimate.

**And the nine years reached one person.** **Ahnentafel 21, Maria Catharina Orešković, born 8 September 1835 at Otočac** — inside the new window, and she had **no reading of her own** although both her parents had been credited from her baptism since it was read. Fixed, and the check that found it is written up in [notes/eight-readings-that-named-nobody.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/eight-readings-that-named-nobody.md).

rows.what: Selce deaths — ahnentafel 48 and 49 read; three ancestors left in the 1790s and 1800s
rows.note:
Row 3 read **ahnentafel 25** (1882) and **ahnentafel 24** (1850, of cholera). **Ahnentafel 48 and 49 are now read too**, both on image **304**, ARK `3:1:3QS7-L99X-1QQL`:

> «*Die **13ᵃ Martii 1829*** · house **51** · ***Joannes Antich Papa**. obiit Annorum **64***»
>
> «*Die **15ᵉ Julii 1829*** · house **56** · ***Margarita uxor Joannis Antich <u>Natanchii</u> obiit Annorum 52***»

**Both dates are the tree's to the day and both ages fit its birth years**, 1765 and 1777. **The houses differ and so do the by-names** — his *Papa*, hers *Natanchii* and **underlined**. One household with two names, a widow moved to a child's house, or two different couples: [the note](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/selce-antic-1829-papa.md) takes none of the three. The marriage, or the Selce *Status Animarum*, would settle it.

**And «Papa» is [question 5](/open-questions/)'s word** — here fifty-six years before the Senj «*Juraj Papa*» and behind a different surname. Not a link between the families: **evidence that *Papa* was a by-name in circulation**, and therefore weak evidence of descent wherever it stands alone.

**Three direct ancestors are left in this book**: ahn **96** (Joannis Antić, 27 Feb 1793), **98** (Pauli Lončarić, 29 Sep 1811) and **99** (Anna Papić, 24 Aug 1807). `targets.json` scores the book **19 reachable of 19** — the only one in the archive where every reachable person is a direct ancestor or their sibling.

**The year map is measured now, and it runs back as well as forward**: 302 = 1828, 304 = 1829, 311 = 1834, 338 = early 1849, 339–340 = Sept–Oct 1850, 341 = 1851–52, 384 = 1877, 397 = 1882 — about **1.7 images to the year** here. **1811 lands near image 273, 1807 near 266, 1793 near 242**, all far outside the measured range, and the film changes books more than once.

**And read the printed page number before writing any negative** — it is in the top outer corner of the right-hand leaf.

---

**20 September 2026 — which books are indexed is now measured rather than assumed.** `sources/familysearch/indexed.psv` holds the table, probed parish by parish through the persona search API. **And the first version of that table was wrong, corrected the same day: marriages and deaths ARE indexed**, through *Hungary, Croatia-Slavonia, Marriages 1678–1927* and *…Deaths 1681–1990*. They were invisible because **the search is ranked and capped** — a broad query returns about sixty rows and whole collections sit below the cut. **Narrow by date and they appear.** **Selce is not indexed at all** — nothing, under Antić, Papić, Jelličić or Lončarić, for any event. **The three remaining ancestors are a film read and there is no shortcut**, which is worth knowing before a sitting rather than during one. Ahnentafel **96 (d. 27 Feb 1793)**, **98 (d. 29 Sep 1811)** and **99 (d. 24 Aug 1807)** all carry exact dates, so the film can be opened at the year and walked.

---

**20 September 2026 — Selce is not unindexed, and this row was planned against a table that said it was.** `indexed.psv` recorded **NOTHING** for Selce, tested «under Antić, Papić, Jelličić and Lončarić». A probe that names **no surname at all** — place plus a date window, reading the returned place string back — finds **five baptisms, 1803–1844**.

**One of them is an ANTIĆ**, which is the surname the zero was recorded under: «Margaritam **Antich**, 7 November 1844, father **Josephi Antich**, mother **Margaritæ**», ark `1:1:QKMJ-MSB9`.

**She is not ahnentafel 12's sister**, and it is worth saying why rather than leaving it to look like one. Ahnentafel 24 IS a Josephus Antić of Selce — but his wife is **Maria Jelličić**, not Margarita, and he died in 1850 with her outliving him to 1882, so there was no second marriage. **A different household.** She is in `found.psv` to be ruled out, because the next reader will meet her first.

**What this row should take from it:** five entries is not a register, and **ahnentafel 48 and 49 were read off the film for good reason**. But the parish is not a blank in the search box, and the three ancestors left in the 1790s and 1800s are worth one place-only probe each before the next sitting is booked. **The place string is bare «Selce, Croatia» with no county — which Selce these five are in is not yet confirmed.** [notes/the-zeros-were-not-all-zeros.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/the-zeros-were-not-all-zeros.md)

rows.what: Karlobag baptisms — one ancestor left, not seven
rows.note:
**This row was written wrong on 15 September and is corrected the same day.** It claimed «seven direct ancestors still unread», taken from the `ahn` list in `targets.json` — but that column names the ancestors a book **could serve**, not the ones still unread. `coverage.json` is the column that answers the question, and it says **seven of the eight are already read**: ahnentafel 13, 26, 27, 52, 54, 55 and 106 all have documents.

**Only ahnentafel 105 is left** — *Catherina «Catta» Luckinić*, born **30 March 1727**, which falls in the **1691–1770** volume.

**And it is a walk, not a lookup.** The index was searched under *Luckinić · Lukinić · Luchinich* and returns **one** Karlobag hit across 900 results — a *Mariu Luketich* of 1756, not her. The 1691–1770 book is not meaningfully indexed for this surname.

**A lesson for every other reading row on this list:** check `coverage.json` before planning a sitting, not `targets.json`. The first says who lacks a document; the second says which book would reach them if they did.

---

**20 September 2026 — this row was wrong in both halves, and the correction is a method.** It has stood since the 15th saying ahnentafel 105 is the last unread Karlobag ancestor and that reaching her «is a walk, not a lookup», the 1691–1770 book being «not meaningfully indexed for this surname».

**She was not unread.** `catherina-catta-luckinic` has held a direct reading — her own death of **29 May 1790**, «Catharina annorum 70, **vidua defti Jacobi [P]ilepich**» — and coverage has graded her `read` accordingly. The row was reporting a gap that had already closed.

**And the book is indexed for this family after all.** Ahnentafel 52's baptism, **11 March 1768**, is in the record index — under **«Josephum PIBERICH»**, father «Jacobi Piberich», mother «Catharina», ark `1:1:QKMX-YX3G`. **«Piberich» returns exactly one record in the whole parish**, so it is not a surname but one clerk's reading of one hand.

**The same couple appear three more times**, as **Pillopich** (Simon, 21 Oct 1758), **Pillepich** (Franciscus, 28 Jul 1762) and **Pillepich** again (Simolicianus, 1 Mar 1765) — all three now in `found.psv` as brothers of ahnentafel 52. **Pillepich is this family's own attested spelling**, from ahnentafel 104's death entry that this archive read itself: «**Pillepich** Jacobus *Capitaneus portûs*».

**What found them was dropping the surname.** Six spellings were tried across three sittings and none was «Piberich», because no list of guesses ever would be. `q.givenName` + `q.fatherGivenName` + `q.motherGivenName` + a date window + the parish returns the household whatever the clerk did to the family name. [notes/karlobag-the-index-calls-them-piberich.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/karlobag-the-index-calls-them-piberich.md)

**Filed `INDEX ONLY`** — no image opened, and the index carries **no surname for the mother**. Catta's Luckinić still comes from the tree.

rows.what: Otočac baptisms 1834–1858 — breadth, not a direct ancestor
rows.note:
**Corrected 15 September 2026, the same way row 26 was.** This row was written citing ahnentafel **10** and **21** from the `ahn` column of `targets.json` — which names who a book *reaches*, not who is *unread*. `coverage.json` says **both are already read**, as are ahn 11 and 20.

**So the value here is breadth, not the direct line:** `targets.json` scores the book **135 people, 91 reachable**, second only to Novi Vinodolski. And it **pays twice**, because this is the book whose *Conditio* column produced the seven Šumećica and Prozor households of [row 1](/worklist/) — every entry read gives a person *and* a house number.

**It is index-led**, which is what makes it cheap: Otočac is indexed for baptisms (165 in the sample), and that is how row 1 was done. **Do it together with [row 51](/worklist/)**, whose two targets — Lucca 1853 and Marija 1858 — sit inside this same book.

**The direct-line work at Otočac is in [row 28](/worklist/), not here.**

---

**20 September 2026 — which books are indexed is now measured rather than assumed.** `sources/familysearch/indexed.psv` holds the table, probed parish by parish through the persona search API. **And the first version of that table was wrong, corrected the same day: marriages and deaths ARE indexed**, through *Hungary, Croatia-Slavonia, Marriages 1678–1927* and *…Deaths 1681–1990*. They were invisible because **the search is ranked and capped** — a broad query returns about sixty rows and whole collections sit below the cut. **Narrow by date and they appear.** **Otočac baptisms are indexed, and by TWO collections rather than one.** *Croatia, Church Books* carries **1839–1846**; **Austria, Küstenland, Births, from 1536 to 1919** carries **1848–1858** — and a searcher who queries only Church Books, as this archive has been doing, misses the whole second half of the book. **That is most of this row's 91 reachable people, and they are a search box rather than a walk.**

---

**20 September 2026 — the households, searched by parents.**

**Ahnentafel 42 × 43, Marcus Orešković and Lucia Sekula**, are indexed under **both** surnames — and the tree already knew, carrying two of their children as *«Orešković Oreskovic **Sekula**»*. A searcher who queries one surname finds half the children. **Two are new**: **Michael, 26 September 1841** and **Paulus, 29 June 1846**.

**Paulus is a twin.** *Petrus*, whom the tree has, was baptised **the same day to the same parents**, on a different ark. [Row 40](/worklist/)'s duplicate detector has a *«same day, same parents»* tier it treats as near-conclusive for one person entered twice — **here it is two boys**, and what separates them is two given names on two arks.

**And the sexes are swapped.** The tree has *Francisca* in **1840** and *Franciscus* in **1844**; the index has **Franciscus 1840** and **Francisca 1844** — same years, same parents, opposite sexes. One is wrong and this archive does not know which.

**Ahnentafel 26 × 27, Vicentius Pilipić and Matia Uroda** — two more the tree lacks: **Maria Catharina, 25 January 1834**, four years before ahnentafel 13, and **Georgius, 18 November 1841**.

**And one household the index cannot reach.** Ahnentafel **40 × 41, Toma Žubrinić and Marija Findrić**: their child was born in **1811** and the Otočac index begins at **1834**. The query returns forty other Žubrinić households and not theirs. **That is coverage, not spelling**, and no surname variation fixes it.

---

**20 September 2026 — the Otočac index has a hard ceiling, and it is this row's own book.** A place-only census, naming no surname:

| births | entries | | births | entries |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1700–1799 | 0 | | 1855–1859 | 200 |
| 1800–1829 | 1 | | **1860–1864** | **0** |
| 1830–1834 | 83 | | **1865–1874** | **0** |
| 1835–1837 | 200 | | **1875–1879** | **0** |

**The index runs 1830–1858 and stops** — which is *this row's book*, «Otočac baptisms 1834–1858», and nothing after it. **So the index and the film cover the same ground**, and this row's «index-led» plan is sound for everything inside it and useless for everything outside.

**It also begins four years EARLIER than the film**, at 1830 rather than 1834. Four years of baptisms are searchable that nobody can open on the roll this archive holds.

**And it is what puts ahnentafel 5 out of reach** — Tereza Žubrinić, born 29 November 1867 at Otočac, Hedviga's paternal grandmother, with only a gravestone. **Outside the index and outside the film**, and so with the post-1894 Senj cases: the parish office or nothing.

rows.what: Otočac deaths — ahnentafel 40 and 41 both read, and a false null corrected
rows.note:
**The best direct-line target at Otočac, now that row 27 is corrected.** Two ancestors are unread and **both have exact death dates inside the filmed 1834–1858 book**:

* **Ahnentafel 40, Toma Žubrinić**, died **4 January 1838** — and the tree places him at ***Šumećica 2***.
* **Ahnentafel 41, Marija Findrić**, died **29 July 1849**.

**Ahn 40 is the one that matters beyond himself.** Šumećica N° 2 is the house where row 1 found Nicolaus Žubrinić baptising children in 1856 and 1858. **A death entry naming that house would tie the direct line to a house number that is currently only inferred** — which is the whole of question 4.

**It is a walk, not a lookup.** Otočac is indexed for **baptisms only** — 165 in the sample and not one death — so the index cannot be used here ([row 43](/worklist/)). The deaths sit on **DGS 5482657**, the same film as the 1846–58 baptisms already read for row 1, so the film is known ground even though the section is not.

**Unblocked and opened, 15 September 2026 — after a sitting lost to the film number.** `…/search/film/005482657?i=N` reports 483 images; **the Otočac book is 218**, and past that the traversal crosses into **Pakrac**, which is why four sampled images were all baptisms and a first conclusion said the deaths were not filmed. They are. Waypoint `9RK1-Y4C:391644801,391674001`; image **100** is 1835, **165** is 1849, **200** is 1855. ARKs in `sources/familysearch/otocac-deaths-1834-1858.json`.

**It is the right instrument.** The far-right column is the running entry number — it restarts at **1** under each ruled year heading — and the entry text carries the village and house — «*Confiniarii e Prozor N° 40*». Exactly what question 4 needs.

**Ahnentafel 41 is read too — image 167, page 153, entry 53.** «*Leta 1849 dne **29 Srpnja** preminula je · **Maria Žubrinić, Udovica** · **69** · Slaboća starosti po dokazu Lečnika · u župničkoj grobnici*». ARK `3:1:3QS7-899C-PVHR`. **The date to the day, the age against the tree's 1780, and the widowhood all agree** — Toma died eleven years earlier. **But no house and no husband are named**, so her entry is not anchored to Šumećica N° 2 the way his is, and this row does not pretend it is.

**And a correction, recorded because it is the useful part.** An earlier pass today read page 151 as ending *28 Srpnja* and page 152 as opening *9 Kolovoza*, and concluded **no death was recorded on 29 July 1849 at all**. Every month in that sentence was wrong: 151 runs **4 *Svibnja* (May) to 8 *Lipnja* (June)**, 152 runs **9 *Lipnja* to 14 *Srpnja* (July)**, and the «*Kate, žena Mate Žubrinića*» entry is **7 May**. July had not been reached. The entry numbers did run continuously — which is what made the wrong conclusion feel safe. **A continuous sequence proves no page is missing; it proves nothing about which months are on it.** Written up in [notes/otocac-marija-findric-1849.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/otocac-marija-findric-1849.md).

**Ahnentafel 40 is read — image 117, page 45, entry 3 of 1838.** «*1838. Januarii die 4ta · **Thomas Xubrinich**, Inq: ~~Ottoèsanq~~ Centu-rio **Confiniarius, ex Pago Shumcchicza N° 2** · **An. 70** · Senectutis Debilitas*». ARK `3:1:3QS7-L99C-PVR4`. **The tree's date, the tree's house and the tree's birth year are all corroborated at once**, for a man who had no media at all. He does not move into house 2 from anywhere — he dies in it, eighteen years before his grandson's children are baptised out of it, and **the «he moved / it is another Nicolaus» pair is no longer level**. Written up in [notes/otocac-toma-zubrinic-1838.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/otocac-toma-zubrinic-1838.md).

**And the book turns out to be worth more than two ancestors.** The Otočac *baptisms* stop writing the household into *Conditio* from about **1836 to 1845**; **the deaths write the village and house straight through those years**. This book is the house-number source for the window the baptisms cannot reach.

rows.what: Senj baptisms 1734–1894 — seventy-three reachable, and ahnentafel 3 and 6
rows.note:
**94 people, 73 reachable**, carrying ahnentafel **3** and **6** — the closest generations to Seka herself that are still unread. The Senj marriage books have been verified end to end, so the parish is known ground; the baptisms have only been sampled. Note the hard edge: **Senj births stop at 1894**, which is what makes questions 1e and 5b unreachable (row 33 of the register's «unreachable» list) and why the Senj parish letter was written.

---

**20 September 2026 — which books are indexed is now measured rather than assumed.** `sources/familysearch/indexed.psv` holds the table, probed parish by parish through the persona search API. **And the first version of that table was wrong, corrected the same day: marriages and deaths ARE indexed**, through *Hungary, Croatia-Slavonia, Marriages 1678–1927* and *…Deaths 1681–1990*. They were invisible because **the search is ranked and capped** — a broad query returns about sixty rows and whole collections sit below the cut. **Narrow by date and they appear.** **Senj baptisms are indexed by THREE collections over one parish** — *Croatia, Lika-Senj, Births* (**1692–1861**), *Croatia, Church Books* (**1735–1857**) and *Hungary, Croatia-Slavonia, Births* (**1807–1851**). The span reaches back to **1692**, which is forty years earlier than this row's book is filmed from. **Ahnentafel 3 and 6 are lookups.** The marriages are not indexed, which is [row 4](/worklist/).

**And the record that disproved the first coverage table is this family's own.** *Hungary, Croatia-Slavonia, Marriages, from 1678 to 1927* holds the **Senj marriage of 4 November 1907** — Zvonimir Vukelić × **Milka Papić**, [question 1c](/open-questions/) — with **both sets of parents**, `1:1:X9D5-DTRW`. His baptism is indexed too, `1:1:X9DP-3Y7X`, **«baptised 25 February 1883 at Senj, Petar Vukelić × Lojza Pulanić»**, confirming to the day what this archive read off the film and confirming that **Lojza and Vjekoslava are one woman**.

**And it disagrees with this archive about her surname.** [Corrections](/corrections/) records that at **5,812 pixels** the 1907 row reads *«† Vjekoslava Putnić»*, with the surname left **unsettled**. The index says **PULANIĆ**, twice, in two different records. Those are not variant spellings — *tn* against *lan*.

**It is not settled in the index's favour, and today is the reason why.** The same indexing names the wrong mother for ahnentafel 106 — *Marie* where the register plainly reads *Antonie*. **An index transcription is not evidence against an image.** What the index adds is that it is **two** transcriptions from two different entries, which makes the question live again without answering it. [notes/senj-1907-vukelic-index.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/senj-1907-vukelic-index.md)

---

**Searched by PARENTS rather than by name, which is the query that finds a household — and it returns five children of ahnentafel 6 and 7.**

| Child | Index | Tree | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Marija | born **11 Aug 1885** | 11 AUG 1885 | agrees to the day |
| **Milka Lucia** | born **9 NOV 1886**, bapt. 17 Nov | **9 OCT 1886** | **DISAGREES — the month** |
| Anica | bapt. **3 Jul 1888** | 25 MAY 1888 | no birth day in the index |
| Josip | bapt. **1890** | 18 MAR 1890 | no day |
| Božica Tonka | born **9 Dec 1891** | 9 DEC 1891 | agrees to the day |

**Milka Lucia Papić is ahnentafel 3** — Hedviga's mother. The day of the month matches and the month is one step out, which is the shape of a transcription slip rather than of two children. **Two things sharpen it**: the index agrees with the tree *to the day* on two of the other four, so it is not careless about this household; and a baptism eight days after a birth is ordinary here, where **thirty-nine days would not be.**

**It is not settled from the index**, for the reason this whole day keeps producing: the same indexing names the wrong mother for ahnentafel 106, and gives Zvonimir Vukelić's mother a surname the archive read differently off the image. **Her own row is deliberately NOT in `readings.psv`** — the four uncontested children are, marked index-only; writing hers in would assert the index over an image that has not been opened.

**And it is reachable.** Senj births are filmed **1878–1894**, so **1886 is inside the film**. **One page settles the archive's second-most-important birth date either way.** [notes/senj-1886-milka-baptism-index.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/senj-1886-milka-baptism-index.md)

**[Question 5b](/open-questions/) is now closed from both directions.** The index holds five of this couple's children and **stops at 1891** — narrowed three ways, the 1895 sisters are not there. Senj births are filmed only to **1894**. **Franjka and Šulka are in neither the book nor the index**, which is what row 29 always said about 1894 and is now tested rather than inferred.

**Tested the same hour against the archive's own images, and the test went against the hypothesis.** The right test does not use the index at all: `sources/readings.psv` records dates read off the pages themselves, and if the tree systematically lost Roman-numeral strokes, **the image reads would show it too**.

**Seventeen dates could be held against the tree. All seventeen agree exactly** — baptisms and deaths, 1754 to 1886, across Karlobag, Otočac, Selce, Senj and Krmpote. **Not one month disagreement, not one day disagreement.**

**And the one that looked like a third case was this archive's own error.** The audit threw up `ivan-blazevic` — tree **25 July 1882**, citation **26 Aug 1882** — the pattern exactly, and against an image rather than an index. **It was the citation that was wrong.** [notes/reading-2026-09-09.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/reading-2026-09-09.md) records the entry as *«1882, 25 / 26 **srpnja**»*, and **srpanj is JULY**. Somebody rendered the Croatian month as August when writing the row. **The tree was right and this archive's data file was not.** Corrected.

**So the weight has moved the other way.** The tree has a perfect record against every image read here, and **both month conflicts are tree against INDEX** — the party already caught twice today naming the wrong person. This note leaned towards the index this morning on a thirty-nine-day gap between birth and baptism. **That gap still wants explaining**, but a transcription with a perfect record and one with two known errors are not equal witnesses.

**Still not settled, and only the page settles it.** Senj births are filmed 1878–1894, so ahnentafel 3's entry is reachable. **One opening decides whether Hedviga's mother was born in October or November.**

---

**20 September 2026 — this row's «ahnentafel 3 and 6 are unread» is now stale in both halves, for different reasons.**

**Ahnentafel 6 is read.** `josip-anton-papic` carries his **baptism of 1 November 1857** and his **marriage of 3 May 1885**, plus a grave and three derived credits. Those rows existed all along but were filed under `josip-anton-JOSO-papic`, **a slug that names nobody**, so every tool skipped them — see [row 16](/worklist/) and [notes/eight-readings-that-named-nobody.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/eight-readings-that-named-nobody.md). Repairing the slug is what made him read.

**Ahnentafel 3 is found and deliberately not recorded.** Her baptism is `1:1:X9D5-SHTB`, Senj, 17 November 1886 — and the index gives her birth as **9 November** where the tree says **9 October**. [notes/senj-1886-milka-baptism-index.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/senj-1886-milka-baptism-index.md) sets out why her row stays out of `readings.psv` until somebody opens the page: writing it in would either assert an index over an image or bury a conflict in a citation. **Senj births are filmed 1878–1894, so one opening settles it.**

**What did come out of the parish today is ahnentafel 7**, at Krivi Put rather than Senj — see [row 31](/worklist/).

rows.what: Senj deaths — all three ancestors read, and the age column exposed
rows.note:
**All three read, 15 September 2026.** Ahnentafel **27** (9 Feb 1886), **8** (26 Jul 1907) and **26** (14 Nov 1897) are each at the page, and every date matches the tree to the day.

**What they add.** Ahn 26 is *«finan.… u miru»* — a **retired finance man**; ahn 8 is a ***nadničar***, a day labourer. Neither had an occupation here before, and the two Senj households sit either side of a line. **Karlobag** is recorded as the origin of *both* ahn 26 and ahn 27, confirming the birthplaces the tree carries and putting the whole couple in Karlobag before Senj. And ahn 8's entry touches **ahnentafel 9** for the first time — *«Udovac iza pok. Tereze»*.

**The finding worth more than the entries: the age column is hearsay, and the clerk says so.** Ahn 26's age is written ***«navodno 93 god.»*** — *reportedly* 93 — against a true 91. Ahn 27's reads 78 against 75. Ahn 8's reads 69 and is exactly right. **An age in this book is what the informant said**, never a document, and it must never be used to date a birth where a baptism exists.

**Two indexing traps recorded.** Ahn 27 is filed under **Pilipić**, her married name — a search for *Uroda* finds nothing. Ahn 26 is filed under **Pilepić**, a different spelling from his own wife's entry in the same office eleven years earlier.

rows.what: Krivi Put baptisms 1847–1884 — fifty-eight reachable, and ahnentafel 7
rows.note:
**100 people, 58 reachable**, carrying ahnentafel **7**. Only one Krivi Put page has ever been opened here (the 1859 baptisms, recorded *partial*). The catalogue range was verified on 14 September, so the book is known to cover the window.

---

**20 September 2026 — which books are indexed is now measured rather than assumed.** `sources/familysearch/indexed.psv` holds the table, probed parish by parish through the persona search API. **And the first version of that table was wrong, corrected the same day: marriages and deaths ARE indexed**, through *Hungary, Croatia-Slavonia, Marriages 1678–1927* and *…Deaths 1681–1990*. They were invisible because **the search is ranked and capped** — a broad query returns about sixty rows and whole collections sit below the cut. **Narrow by date and they appear.** **Krivi Put IS indexed — and the first probe said it was not.** Searched under **Prpić**, this parish returns gravestones and nothing else. Searched under **Tomljanović**, it returns **30 indexed baptisms, 1850–1870**, in *Hungary, Croatia-Slavonia, Births*. **A single surname can miss an entire collection**, and this row's own surname is the one that misses it.

**And there is a death index here, the only parish register death index in the table**: *Hungary, Croatia-Slavonia, Deaths*, **1891–1924**. Too late for ahnentafel 7's baptism, and not too late for her death.

---

**20 September 2026 — searched by parents, and the household came out.**

**Ahnentafel 14 × 15, Joannes Perpić and Lucia**, at Krivi Put. The index writes her **«Lucia Perpić»** — **independent corroboration of [question 5c](/open-questions/)**, which recovered her surname off the 1885 marriage at nine times magnification as *«Luca rodjena Pèr-pić»* and concluded **she is a Prpić who married a Prpić**. The index agrees, from a different document.

**Three children the tree does not have** — Georgius **22 April 1868**, Joanna **6 January 1874**, Josephus **7 July 1876** — all recorded in `found.psv` as **candidates**, because Prpić is the dominant surname of this parish and the index holds several *Perpić × Perpić* couples. What supports them is that **the same couple's Stephanus of 1861 is in the tree.**

**And he brought a second date conflict of exactly the shape Milka's has.** The tree gives Stephanus **13 OCTOBER 1861**; the index gives **13 December 1861**, baptised the 16th. **The day survives, the month does not, and the tree's month is the earlier one — as it was for ahnentafel 3.** Four other dates from the same sweep agree exactly.

**A mechanism, offered as a hypothesis**: these registers write the month as a **Roman numeral**, and both errors are the same error — *XI → X* and *XII → X*, the trailing strokes lost. That would preserve the day, corrupt only the month, and could only ever make the month **earlier**. **It predicts a direction**, so it is testable: the tree's month should never be *later*, and the disagreements should cluster in October, November and December. Six comparisons is a shape, not a test. [notes/the-month-is-wrong-and-the-day-is-right.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/the-month-is-wrong-and-the-day-is-right.md)

**And the Roman-numeral hypothesis did not survive the test** — see [row 29](/worklist/). Seventeen image-read dates agree with the tree exactly; both month conflicts are against the INDEX, not against a page. Stephanus's **13 October 1861** is more likely right than the index's 13 December.

---

**20 September 2026 — ahnentafel 7's own entry was in the result set that produced her brothers, and it was passed over.** `found.psv` has carried **Georgius 1868**, **Joanna 1874** and **Josephus 1876** as candidate siblings since this morning, and **Stephanus 1861** is quoted in the month note. **Antonija «Tonka» Perpić had a gravestone, four derived credits, and no entry of her own.**

    Birth 12 May 1859 · Baptism 15 May 1859 · Krivi Put
    Father «Joannis Perpić»  Mother «Luciæ Perpić»  ·  ark 1:1:XQM9-6NQ4

**It agrees with the tree to the day**, and the three-day gap to baptism is ordinary here — which is a third data point saying this index is not careless about this family, against the two entries that disagree with the tree by a month.

**It gives ahnentafel 15 her first document of any kind.** She had none. It does **not** give her a maiden name: the Krivi Put index writes every mother under the father's surname, so «Luciæ Perpić» is a convention.

**Two more candidate elder siblings** into `found.psv` — **Martha 1853** and **Toma 1856** — both flagged CANDIDATE, because at least two Joannes Perpić households sit at Krivi Put in this decade and one of them is married to a Francisca. [notes/the-household-was-swept-and-she-was-left-out.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/the-household-was-swept-and-she-was-left-out.md)

rows.what: Novi Vinodolski 1650–1900 — the largest reach in the archive, and no ancestor in it
rows.note:
**132 people, 120 reachable — the highest count of any book here — and not one direct ancestor.** That combination is exactly why it keeps being deferred, and exactly why it should be done deliberately rather than by accident: it is **breadth, not depth**, and it would settle a great many collateral lines at once. It is also the **earliest register in the estate** — the 1650 book was opened once and its earliest leaves are in **Croatian, not Latin**, which is a finding in its own right. Do it when the direct line is exhausted, or when a wet afternoon wants volume.

---

**20 September 2026 — which books are indexed is now measured rather than assumed.** `sources/familysearch/indexed.psv` holds the table, probed parish by parish through the persona search API. **And the first version of that table was wrong, corrected the same day: marriages and deaths ARE indexed**, through *Hungary, Croatia-Slavonia, Marriages 1678–1927* and *…Deaths 1681–1990*. They were invisible because **the search is ranked and capped** — a broad query returns about sixty rows and whole collections sit below the cut. **Narrow by date and they appear.** **Novi Vinodolski baptisms are indexed, 1826–1899**, in *Hungary, Croatia-Slavonia, Births*. This row has been deferred for months as *«the largest reach in the archive»* — 132 people, 120 reachable — on the assumption that it meant opening the earliest register in the estate. **For the nineteenth century it does not: it is a search box.** The 1650–1825 stretch is still a walk, and that is where the row's «earliest register» value lies.

---

**20 September 2026 — this book is indexed far wider than the coverage table said, and it is Klenovica's parish.** `indexed.psv` recorded Novi Vinodolski as *baptism, probed 1680s 1850s*. A place-only census, naming no surname:

| births | entries | | births | entries |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1650–1749 | **300 of 300** | | 1830–1859 | **300 of 300** |
| 1750–1799 | **300 of 300** | | 1860–1879 | **300**, baptisms **and burials** |
| 1800–1829 | **300 of 300** | | 1880–1899 | **300**, baptisms **and burials** |

**Dense in every window from 1651 to 1899**, and **burials are indexed from 1860** — about a quarter of the rows in the last two windows and none before. A book recorded as sampled in two decades is searchable across two and a half centuries.

**And it is the Kalanj parish.** `parishes.psv` gives Novi Vinodolski as *novi vinodolski, klenovica, povile*, and **101 of this archive's people are at Klenovica**. This row says «no ancestor in it» — true of the direct line, and it undersells what is here.

**It has already produced one.** `corrections.json` records **four** Kalanj baptisms «sitting unattached in the family's own photo library». **The index holds five**: a **Rozalia Kalanj, baptised 5 August 1893**, ark `1:1:XQMQ-QY3Q`, same parents — and `rozalia-kalanj` is in the tree with **no reading of any kind**, because hers is the one scan nobody had. **The four that were in the library got read; the fifth was never looked for.** Filed INDEX ONLY and flagged: the tree gives her birth as 4 July and the index her baptism as 5 August, a month where her siblings' entries put days.

[notes/novi-vinodolski-is-indexed-to-1899.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/novi-vinodolski-is-indexed-to-1899.md)

**And then the opening closed, the same afternoon.** A densely indexed parish holding 101 of this archive's people looked like the best lead of the day. **It is not.** The **Kalanj surname appears FIVE times in the whole Novi Vinodolski index** — eight spellings tried, as surname and as father's surname — and all five are the one household of Martin Kalanj and Marija Peričić, **1893 to 1900. Nothing earlier, nothing else.**

**It is not surname-blindness**, and it was tested the way that fault is tested. *Father Josephus × mother Rosalia, 1855–1870* — the household whose baptisms `corrections.json` quotes off the page — returns **0**. *Josephus, 1824–1828* returns **24** dense Novi Vinodolski baptisms: Sokolić, Krišković, Maričić, Petrinović, Karlović, Potočnjak, Piskulić, Radetić **and Peričić**. **Peričić is in the index and Kalanj is not**, same parish, same decade. **The index for this parish does not hold this family before 1893.**

**And the village is invisible.** «Klenovica» as a place returns **Cres, Hreljin, Lopar** — other parishes entirely; *Povile* the same. Every row here is filed **«Novi Vinodolski»**, 200 of 200 in the 1800–1860 sample. **Search the parish, never the village.**

**So this row stays a film read** — baptisms 1650–1900, marriages 1674–1859, deaths 1704–1899 per `parishes.psv` — in a parish whose index is dense for everybody except us. **The five indexed entries are the end of what the search box can do here, not the beginning.**

rows.what: Krmpote-Vodice and Ledenice births — the Blažević side
rows.note:
The two Blažević ancestors without a document, **ahn 16 (Anton) and ahn 32 (Ilija, b. 1790)**, are both placed at **Smokvica Krmpotska**. Krmpote-Vodice births score 15 reachable and Ledenice 15 more. **The trap is recorded and must be respected**: Krmpote's catalogue label says 1815 and **the film actually begins in 1879** — verified by opening it — so Ilija of 1790 is *not* in it. Ledenice (1734–1894) is the book that could hold him, and Krmpote is administered from Ledenice to this day.

---

**20 September 2026 — which books are indexed is now measured rather than assumed.** `sources/familysearch/indexed.psv` holds the table, probed parish by parish through the persona search API. **And the first version of that table was wrong, corrected the same day: marriages and deaths ARE indexed**, through *Hungary, Croatia-Slavonia, Marriages 1678–1927* and *…Deaths 1681–1990*. They were invisible because **the search is ranked and capped** — a broad query returns about sixty rows and whole collections sit below the cut. **Narrow by date and they appear.** **Krmpote is indexed 1880–1894 — and the index confirms the trap this row records.** The catalogue label says the film begins in **1815**; this row already established by opening it that it actually begins in **1879**. The index agrees with the film and not the catalogue. **Ahnentafel 32, Ilija, born 1790, is not reachable by index or by film**, and Ledenice returns nothing indexed at all.

---

**20 September 2026 — re-tested with the date-window method, and the answer is firm.**

The first coverage pass probed broadly and I had to correct it within the hour, because **a broad query is ranked and capped and whole collections hide below the cut**. So Ledenice was left in `indexed.psv` marked *«broadly probed only — re-test by window»*.

**Re-tested, under Blažević and Tomljanović, across 1730–1800, 1800–1850 and 1850–1900: Ledenice returns nothing at all.** Krmpote returns only the 1850s window, matching the **1880–1894** already observed and the film that begins in **1879** rather than the catalogue's 1815. **Smokvica Krmpotska returns nothing** under Blažević.

**So ahnentafel 16 and 32 cannot be reached from a search box, and this row is a film read** — now measured twice by two methods rather than assumed.

**And the shape of the whole thing is worth naming.** The indexing in this archive's country is a **Karlobag–Otočac–Senj phenomenon**. Those three are indexed deeply, by several collections each, back to the seventeenth century. **Smokvica, Krmpote before 1880, Ledenice, Selce, Brinje, Bribir, Sinac and Gospić are not indexed at all.** Hedviga's **mother's** side is searchable and her **father's** side is not — which is why every finding of the last two days has been a Papić, a Pilipić, an Uroda or a Žubrinić, and not one has been a Blažević.

---

**And the one Blažević-side window that IS indexed was searched — Krmpote 1880–1894 — with two results, one of them about [question 1b](/open-questions/).**

**The index gives Marijan Blažević the wrong father.** It holds `1:1:XQMS-HRQW` — *«Marijan Blažević, baptism 1895 Krmpote-Vodice, birth Dec 1895, **Ivko** Blažević × Tereza Zubrinić»*. This archive read the same entry off the image on 9 September: **p.168 no.26, «1895, travnja 12 / 16»** — *travanj is April* — parents ***«Jurko Blažević i Tereza rođ. Žubrinić, selj.»***, **Smokvica kbr. 114**.

**It is one entry, not two** — two entries would need two women called Tereza Žubrinić married to two Blažević men in one small parish, each naming a son Marijan in 1895.

**And the entry shows how the name went wrong. The GODFATHER is «Ive Blažević, sin Tomin».** Both names are on the line, and the index has put **Ive** in the father's slot. That is a mechanism rather than a guess, and it leaves the image read intact — with the house number and the occupation the index does not carry.

**It changes nothing in question 1b, which is the point of checking.** But **anybody searching the index rather than the film will be told Marijan's father was an Ivan, and will not find Juraj at all.** [notes/krmpote-1895-the-index-took-the-godfather.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/krmpote-1895-the-index-took-the-godfather.md)

**And the negative: Ljubomir (1892) and Anka (1893) are both inside the indexed window and neither baptism is there.** The only Ljubomir entry anywhere is his **1920 marriage**, the only Anka entry her **1919 marriage**. The couple's two eldest are **not in the Krmpote baptism index even where it covers their years** — consistent with [question 13](/open-questions/), which argues from the other direction that **Ljubomir was baptised at Rijeka**.

---

**20 September 2026 — Ledenice is not a zero either, and it is still a film read.** Both halves matter. `indexed.psv` said **NOTHING** for Ledenice, tested under Blažević and Tomljanović. A surname-free place probe finds **four entries across two centuries**: 1748, 1749, 1845 and 1888. **That is not a register**, and this row's plan does not change — **Smokvica is still zero and Krmpote before 1880 is still zero**, so the Blažević side remains unreachable from a search box.

**But the 1888 one paid.** «**Marija Milka**, 16 May 1888, Ledenice, parents **Luka Kalanj** and **Kata**», ark `1:1:XQM9-8KKX` — and `marija-milka-kalanj` is **in the tree**, carrying the bare year *1888* and a citation to the register image. **The index supplies the day the tree does not have.** Filed `INDEX ONLY`; the index gives her mother the father's surname where the tree has *Kata Miletić*, which is an indexing convention rather than a conflict.

**And a caution this row should carry.** The same place-only probe returned **zero for Krmpote in every window** — while this archive found an indexed Krmpote-Vodice baptism of 1895 by surname on the same day. **Neither probe is authoritative alone.** A zero from either means «not found by this instrument».

rows.what: Twenty-one ancestors with no place — and the last four had a grandchild all along
rows.note:
Of the **34 direct ancestors without a document**, **21 have no place recorded — not a village, not a parish, in several cases not a date either**: ahn 22, 41, 64, 80, 84, 85, 86, 87, 97, 100, 101, 102, 103, 109, 128, 210, 211, 213, 427, 428, 429. **No amount of film-reading reaches them**, because nothing says which film to open. This row is the precondition for half the rows above it.

The method that works is the one that found ahnentafel 55's father: **a person with no record of their own is named in their child's**. Every one of these twenty-one has a child in the tree; the child's baptism or marriage entry names the parent and usually the village. So the job is to **work down from the children**, not up from the parents.

---

**Two came off the list on 15 September without any film being opened, because they were never placeless.**

The list was built from the wall grading, and the wall grading called a household **«No place recorded»** whenever no parish in `parishes.psv` claimed its village. That is not the same thing. The tree gives **ahnentafel 426** as born at **Smiljan, Općina Gospić** and **ahnentafel 222** at **Montani Stanište** — both written plainly, both printed for weeks under «*No place is recorded for this household anywhere on the line*».

**`walls.py` now separates the two**, with a new grade **`ungazetteered`** — *«The tree does record where this household was … but no parish in this archive's table claims that village … This is not a wall in the record. It is a gap in the gazetteer.»* **Nineteen of the twenty-one are genuinely placeless. Two are one line of `parishes.psv` away**, and that line is [row 56](/worklist/).

**A third came off earlier the same day**: ahnentafel **220**, placed at Karlobag by his own death entry. So the twenty-one is **eighteen**, and the method the row proposed — *work down from the children* — has not been started yet.

---

**Three more came off the list on 15 September, and again no film was opened.** The wall grading looked at **one field on two people** — the person's own `bornPlace`, then the ahnentafel child's — and called everything else *«No place is recorded for this household anywhere on the line»*. That sentence was false three more times.

* **Ahnentafel 102, Joanni Brozović** — his daughter Margarita is recorded as **dying at Selce**. A death place is a place.
* **Ahnentafel 103, Catharina**, his wife — the same daughter, the same parish.
* **Ahnentafel 427, Mara Pekass** — her husband is recorded as **born at Smiljan**, and the grading never once looked at a spouse, though it had been computing one all along. **A husband's parish is his wife's.**

**The fallback now runs through the household, nearest first** — own death, child's birth, child's death, spouse's birth, spouse's death — and **each wall says which relation supplied it**: *«This household is put at Selce on the strength of their child's death — the tree's own words about the tree's own people, not a document.»* That distinction is the whole point. Nothing here was read off a page, and a wall that pretended otherwise would be worse than one that said nothing.

**Four are genuinely placeless and always were**: **ahnentafel 84 and 86, Vitus and Michael Sekula**; **128, Mateša Blažević**; **428, Angelo Bacchi**. Not a village, not a death place, not a spouse, not a child with either. For these four the row's original method — work down from the children's baptisms — is still the only way in, and it still needs a register.

---

**17 September 2026 — and the four «genuinely placeless» were three fields short, not a register short.**

The fallback ran **own death → child's birth → child's death → spouse's birth → spouse's death** and stopped. It stopped **one generation too early**, and «*no place is recorded for this household anywhere on the line*» was false a third time — over the very sentence that says *on the line*.

* **Ahnentafel 128, Mateša Blažević** — his grandson **Ilija is born at Smokvica Krmpotska**, written plainly in the tree.
* **Ahnentafel 84, 85, 86 and 87 — Vitus and Michael Sekula and their two wives called Maria** — all four are grandparents of **ahnentafel 21, born at Otočac**. One person's birthplace places four walls.
* **Ahnentafel 428, Angelo Bacchi**, and **429, Catharina** — their granddaughter **Oliva Andreana Bacchi dies at Karlobag**.

**The grandchild goes last in the chain because it is the weakest**, and each wall says so in the same words the others use: *«This household is put at Karlobag on the strength of their grandchild's death — the tree's own words about the tree's own people, not a document.»* Nothing was read off a page.

**Unplaced went from four to none — and two of them are now reachable books.** Angelo Bacchi's baptism of about **1752** and his marriage to Catharina of about **1777** both fall **inside** Karlobag, which is filmed 1691–1861 **and indexed** — that is [row 54](/worklist/)'s finding. Catharina has no surname at all, and a marriage entry is what supplies one. **Two walls moved from «nothing is known» to «a book this archive already knows how to read».**

The rest are honest silences: 84, 85, 86, 87 want Otočac before **1834**, and 128 wants Krmpote before **1879**. Neither film goes back that far.

rows.what: Gologorica — handed to the Defranceschi archive, because the Šestani were never this archive's family
rows.note:
**Founded on a mistake, and kept here rather than deleted — the mistake was in the scope, not in the work.**

This row asked which register serves **Gologorica**, where `targets.json` puts **23 Šestani**. Two sittings went into it. Nobody asked the prior question: **why is a Šestan row in a Blažević archive?**

**It is not one.** `tools/ancestry.py` carries eight surnames and `sestan` is among them, so 55 Šestani are published — but:

* **Twenty-five of the fifty-five have a DEFRANCESCHI mother** — Joanna (10 children), Sancta-Alexandra (9), Rosa (6).
* **No Šestan connects to Hedviga through any published person at all.** In the full 15,643-person tree the nearest is **ten steps** away:

  `Hedviga → married Ivan Anton Defranceski → up five Defranceschi generations → (unnamed) → «Grah's for Investigation (not real)» → «Gologorica Grah» → Josephus Grah 1864 → married Rosa Sestan 1872`

* **Two of those links are sorting buckets**, and one of them — *«Grah's for Investigation (not real)»* — this archive's own `buckets.py` already classifies as not a person.

**So they are reached through Hedviga's HUSBAND's family, and then only through a node the archive itself says is not real.** The Defranceschi archive's own queue had the corroboration waiting: Forebears gives Gračišće's surnames as *Jugovac 489, **Šestan 316**, Pauro 234* — **Šestan is the second commonest surname in that village.**

**Handed over 20 September 2026** to `TheDefranceski`, commit `1cbcea8`, appended to their `notes/QUEUE.md`: that Gologorica is not a catalogued parish and the zero was tested against a nonsense control; that **Pazin's book reaches 1582** (`koha:725172`) with the film numbers; that the Šestan baptisms are **indexed under PISINO and invisible under Pazin**; that nothing yet places the 23 Gologorica Šestani in that book, so the film is **not yet worth a sitting**; and two free people — a death and a married name for **Elisabetha Sestan**, and **«Gologorica Grah»**, a village name sitting in a given-name field.

**One thing is left open and is not this archive's to decide**: whether **`sestan` should stay in the eight-surname scope list**. Taking it out would unpublish 55 people. It is recorded in [the sister-archive notes](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/for-the-sister-archives.md) rather than acted on.

---

**What the two sittings actually found, kept because it is true and was paid for:**

`parishes.psv` carries **Gologorica** with *unknown* in all three range columns and the note «Istria — likely a different collection entirely». `targets.json` puts **23 people** behind it. It is the only parish in the table that has never been resolved at all. One catalogue search decides whether it is reachable or whether it joins the unreachable list honestly.

---

**Half answered, 15 September 2026, and the half that is answered changes its priority.**

**Every one of the 24 people behind Gologorica is a Šestan, and not one of them is a direct ancestor.** The parish stands entirely on a married-in line. That does not make it worthless — it makes it **the last of the twenty-one parishes to spend a day on**, not the outstanding hole the row implies.

**The catalogue question is still open and could not be answered from here.** The catalogue's own search service refuses every parameter this archive knows how to send (`q.text`, `q.placeText`, `q.anyPlace` all return 400; the UI's own call to `/service/search/catalog/v3/search` returns 400 too and the page prints *«Something Went Wrong»*). **The place search wants a place id**, not a name, and getting one needs the typeahead the interface uses.

**So the row stays open with a smaller question**: not *«is Gologorica reachable»* but *«which collection holds Istrian parish registers, and is it this one»* — and it can wait behind every row that touches the direct line.

---

**20 September 2026 — the one catalogue search, done. The answer is neither «reachable» nor «unreachable».**

**Gologorica is not a catalogued parish.** Searched under four forms — *Gologorica*, *Gollogorizza*, *Gologorizza*, and the modern municipality *Cerovlje* — all empty.

**And the zero was tested rather than assumed**, because this catalogue pads every result with a **constant filler list**: a Staffordshire map, a Wagler family history, a Hungarian church in Hamilton. Thirty rows come back whatever you ask.

| query | result |
|---|---|
| `Karlobag` | **koha:655222 «Matična knjiga, 1691-1861»**, then filler |
| `Gologorica` | filler only |
| `zzzzqqqnotaplace` | filler only — **byte-identical to Gologorica** |

**But the district town is catalogued, and its book is extraordinary.** `koha:725172` — **«Matična knjiga, 1582-1882»**, filmed from the Hrvatski državni arhiv: **births 1582–1882, marriages 1597–1852, deaths 1655–1847**, with `koha:725059` adding births 1656–1822.

**Births from 1582.** The earliest this archive has reached until today is **Novi Vinodolski, 1650** — which [row 32](/worklist/) calls *«the earliest register in the estate»*. **Pazin is sixty-eight years older.**

**And the catalogue note is the sovereignty problem in one sentence**: *«for **Mitterburg, Küstenland, Austria**; later **Pisino, Istria, Italy**; now **Pazin, Croatia**»* — one parish filed under three countries and three names. This archive met the same thing from the other end four days ago, when one man gave *«Zara, Austria»* in 1919 and *«Italy»* in 1924 because Rapallo happened in between. **A searcher who knows only the Croatian name finds a third of this parish.**

**`parishes.psv` now carries Pazin** in place of the unresolved Gologorica row. **What is NOT established is that the Šestani were written into it** — a village ten kilometres from a district town may have had its own chapel or belonged to a nearer parish that is itself uncatalogued. [notes/gologorica-is-not-a-parish-but-pazin-is.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/gologorica-is-not-a-parish-but-pazin-is.md)

**And the index was then asked what the catalogue could not answer — is Pazin's book the Šestani's book? There is no evidence that it is.**

**The Šestani ARE indexed at Pazin, in the eighteenth century** — searched as **Pisino**: births **1795, 1804, 1807, 1826, 1827, 1834**, deaths back to *Joannes Sestan, born 1659, died 23 April 1709*, marriages from 1787. **Searched as «Pazin» those births do not appear at all** — the collection is filed under the Austrian name. **That is the three-names problem costing a searcher two thirds of a parish**, shown on this family's own surname.

**But not one of this archive's Šestani is among them.** `targets.json` puts **23 Šestani at Gologorica, born 1843–1877**. In that window the index returns Šestani at **Poreč, Rovinj, Pola, Ližnjan and Vrsar** — and **none at Gologorica, none at Pazin**. **Šestan is an Istrian surname spread across the peninsula**: the Kalanj lesson and the Perpić lesson a third time.

**So: the Pazin film is available and is not yet worth a sitting.** Writing that down is the point — without it the next reader sees *1582* and spends a day on a book that may have nothing to do with this family.

**One record does put a Šestan at Gologorica, and it is American**: *Elisabetta Sestan Rabar*, born **11 July 1912** at *«Gologorica I\*, Yugoslavia»*, died Staten Island 2005, parents *Natale Sestan × Antonia Ancich*. **The village is real and people were born there. It is the parish register that is missing, not the place.**

**And a loose thread kept rather than tidied**: *«23 March 1842, **Otočac** — Johanna Sestan, of Philippus Sestan × Martha»*. A Šestan baptised in **Lika**, three hundred kilometres from Istria, in this archive's own heartland. Nothing is built on it.

---

**And the last question was the one nobody had asked: whose family is this?**

**Twenty-five of the fifty-five Šestani in this tree have a DEFRANCESCHI mother.** Three women — **Joanna** (10 children), **Sancta-Alexandra** (9), **Rosa** (6).

**The Šestani are here because three Defranceschi women married Šestan men.** They are not a Blažević family and not a Lika one, and the 23 at Gologorica are this archive's people only by marriage.

**Which makes this the Defranceschi archive's row.** That archive works **Gračišće and the county of Pazin** — the same district as Gologorica, the same `koha:725172` from **1582**, the same Mitterburg / Pisino / Pazin problem. **Everything found here today is more use to it than to this one**: that the village is not a catalogued parish, that the district book reaches 1582, that the births are filed under the Austrian name and invisible under the Croatian one, and that Šestan is a peninsula-wide surname.

**This archive does not hand work away silently**, so the row says so rather than being struck. The owner is now *«this archive, and then Defranceschi»*.

**One person gained a death and a husband on the way past — and it is a rediscovery, which is worth admitting.** The American record offered above as *«one record does put a Šestan at Gologorica»* is **somebody this tree already holds**: `elisabetha-sestan-3`, **Elisabetha Sestan, born 11 July 1912**, of *Natalis Joannes Sestan × Antonia Ancic*. rows.what: Duplicate groups — and the tool was only looking at one end of a life
rows.note:
`duplicates.json`: **51 groups**, of which **23 are live** and 28 already rejected. A live duplicate group is two tree records that may be one person — which is the same question as the two Georgius Urode and the seven Michaels, and it now has a settled method. **28 have already been rejected**, so the remaining 23 are the hard ones and deserve the register rather than judgement.

---

**Worked 15 September 2026. Six of the twenty-three are settled, and the tool had only half a test.**

`duplicates.py` had **`parents_conflict`** — a veto that rejects a group when two records name parents sharing no name. It had **no confirmation**: two records naming *the same* parents stayed «live» exactly like two naming nobody. So a new tier, **`same day and same parents`**, and **five groups fall into it** — same birth day, same village, same father, same mother, nothing left for a second child to be:

| Who | Born | Parents |
|---|---|---|
| Catharina Žubrinić | 20 Nov 1840, Otočac | Mate × Anna Mudrovčić |
| Josephus Žubrinić | 16 Mar 1845, Otočac | Michael × Maria Marković |
| Francisca Žubrinić | 6 Mar 1846, Otočac | Thomas × Joanna Ratković |
| Nicolaus Žubrinić | 3 Aug 1847 | Thomas × Joanna Ratković |
| Katalyn / Kate Zubrinich | 26 Jul 1886, Port Pirie | John × Rose Gormley |

**And Danijel Kalanj, 2 November 1829, Klenovica** is the plainest of all without qualifying: one copy carries his parents, the other his wife and child, and **both carry the same death date, 26 June 1876**. One man, entered twice, split down the middle.

**The sixth is not a duplicate at all, and finding that out is the point.** «*Alexander Žubrinić, 14 March 1839, Otočac*» has the same day and the same village and a **Michael** for a father in both — and the mothers are **Magdalena Orešković** and **Magdalena Mande Draženović**. Two boys, born the same day, to two different Michaels. **It is [row 1](/worklist/)'s seven Michaels in miniature**, and the first draft of the new tier declared it a duplicate, because `parents()` folds a parent to their **given names only** and both mothers reduce to *magdalena*. `parent_surnames()` now supplies the half of the name that was being thrown away.

**And the house number cannot rescue it.** Alexander is 1839, and this archive established that the Otočac baptisms **stop writing the household into *Conditio* from about 1836 to 1845**. The one instrument that separates Michaels does not reach the years where they most need separating. **The 1834–1858 deaths do carry it** — that is [row 28](/worklist/)'s finding — so the way in is a death, not a baptism.

**Seventeen groups remain**: eight *same year and place*, eight *same year only*, one *same day*. They are the hard ones, as the row said.

---

**A second sitting, and the tool had a second blind spot — this one in its keys.**

Every group above is found by keying on a **surname and a given name**, so two records can only meet if somebody spelled them alike. **pava Boras** and **Paulina Boras** never meet: the two strings share two letters and no token, so containment fails and the three-letter-prefix rule fails with it. **They are one woman.** Born **24 December 1895**, the same parents, and both married an **Ivan Krmpotić** — one copy carrying the marriage, 1917 at Senj, and no children; the other seven children and no marriage date. That is precisely the split Danijel Kalanj shows, and it was invisible.

**So a pass was added that never looks at the name.** It starts from the family: children of one couple who share an **exact birth date**. On its own that proves nothing — **this tree holds 113 such pairs** and most of them are twins, several labelled so in the tree itself. **The discriminator is the marriage. Twins do not marry the same person; a record entered twice does.**

**And it has to be the spouse's NAME, not their record.** Matching on ids found one pair and missed the Borases, because the tree holds **two Ivan Krmpotićs** — duplicating a wife duplicates her husband along with her. On names it fires **eight times** across 15,643 people, with no twin among them. Seven are married-in South African and Welsh lines; **the Borases are the only one in the Croatian material**, which is a statement about where the tree was built carelessly, not about where this pass works.

**Two tiers were being counted and never shown.** `same day and same parents` — the five groups this row added on the first sitting — was never added to `/duplicates`, so the page's total said thirteen while its tables listed eight. Both new tiers are on the page now. **A tier the reader cannot see is worse than no tier at all.**

---

**A third sitting, 17 September 2026, and the blind spot this time was chronological.**

Every test the tool had was built on a **birth**: the birth day, the birth year, the birth place. Nothing anywhere in it looked at the **death**. That had already been written down as a problem and left — this row's own note says of Danijel Kalanj, *«the plainest of all without qualifying»*, that **both his records carry the same death date, 26 June 1876**, and he sat in the bare «same day» tier anyway because nothing could see it.

**Two changes, and they are the same idea applied twice.**

**A confirmation, `same day, and the same death day`.** One person dies once and on one day. It is a confirmation of the same weight as *same parents* — and better in one way, because **siblings share parents and cannot share a death day**. It fires once, on Danijel Kalanj, which is exactly the case the row had already identified and could not grade.

**And the name-blind pass now runs on the death date too.** Keying on the birth day finds a record split down the middle when both halves kept the birth. It cannot find **Louis Barry**, who is in this tree **twice with two different birth years — 17 February 1920 and 1907** — so no key built from a name and a year could ever put his two records in one bucket. What they share is the day he died: **20 March 1983 at Cape Town**, both born at Elliot, both married to **Louise Sophie van Heerden**. **Live groups 31 → 32.**

**One veto, and it earned its place immediately.** Two records that both carry a full birth date and **disagree** about it are two people whatever else they share. **Elizabeth Margaretha Catharina Botha** (b. 29 January 1797) and **Margaretha Debora Maria Botha** (b. 15 May 1802) are sisters who both married a **George Aldric** and are both entered as dying on **15 March 1889**. Without the veto the pass would have announced her as one woman. She is two, and the coincidence is recorded rather than resolved.

**And a latent false claim closed on the way past.** `full_date` tested a date by its *length*, so **«FEB 1967» passed as a day** and would have been graded «*same day. Near-conclusive.*» No group published here ever rested on one — checked before the rule was tightened — so nothing was re-graded. The door is shut.

**Both tiers are on [/duplicates](/duplicates/).** That rule was learned last sitting and is not being broken this one.

---

**20 September 2026 — the index reaches the duplicates at last, and it answers two of them.**

A live group is **two tree records that may be one person**, and the register settles it with one question: **is there one baptism entry, or two?** Four of the seventeen fall inside the Otočac index's window of 1834–1858.

**Andreas Žubrinić, 1844 — one entry, and one of the two records is a fragment.** The tree has `andreas-zubrinic` (**13 Nov 1844**, Otočac, Michael × Catharina) and `andreas-zubrinic-xubrinich` (**Nov 1844**, no day, no place, same two parents' given names). **The index holds exactly one baptism** — 13 November 1844, «Michaël Žubrinić × Catharina», `1:1:QKMK-S6M9`. **One copy has the day and the place and the other has neither**: the shape of **Danijel Kalanj** and of **pava / Paulina Boras**, one record entered twice.

**Alexander Žubrinić, 1839 — and the register does not give the mother a surname.** This row has said since the 15th that these are *«two boys, born the same day, to two different Michaels»*, and `duplicates.py` grew **`parent_surnames()`** precisely so that *Orešković* and *Draženović* would keep them apart.

**Those two surnames are not in the register.** The index holds **one** baptism — 14 March 1839, «Michael Žubrinić × **Magdalena**», `1:1:QKMK-STYY` — **and the mother has no surname in it.** Whatever supplied *Orešković* to one record and *Draženović* to the other, it was not this baptism.

**So the discriminator is working on data that is not evidence.** That does not make them one boy. It means **the reason given for their being two does not come from a document**, and this row should stop repeating it as though it did.

**And the caution is the same one that keeps recurring: the index is not complete.** The measure is Karlobag, where the entire Luckinić holding is **seven entries** for a family documented across generations, and ahnentafel 105's own baptism is missing while her father's other children are there. **«The index holds one entry» is not «the register holds one entry»** — though in the Alexander case it does something stronger than point: it removes the grounds for the opposite conclusion.
