[notes/the-index-and-the-duplicates.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/the-index-and-the-duplicates.md)

**Two of the four were not answered**: *Lucia 1835* returns nothing at Otočac, and *Magdalena 1847* returns one entry to Philippus × Maria Begović, which is neither of the pair.

---

**And then the index found four groups that are one household — which exposed a tier this tool never had.**

Krivi Put holds **one couple, Antonius Blažević × Maria Šojat**, producing exactly the four names that make four separate duplicate groups: **Ivan 10 Aug 1853, Mile 8 Sep 1855, Marko 27 Mar 1863, Ane 30 Oct 1865** — one indexed baptism each.

**In the tree those four are nine records, and every one names the same two parents under three spellings apiece** — *Antona / Antone / **Anton Kljapo** Blažević* and *Marija Sojat / Mare Sojat / **Marija Šojat***. `parents_agree()` already returns **True** for all four. They could not reach the confirming tier for one reason only: **it requires a full birth date on EVERY record**, and in each group one copy carries a year and nothing else.

**That is the commonest shape a split record takes** — one complete copy with a day, a village and sometimes a house number, and one stub with a year and two parents. **Danijel Kalanj is that shape. So is pava Boras. So is Andreas Žubrinić.** And it was invisible, scattered across the two weakest tiers where the fact that the parents agree could not be seen.

**New tier: «same year, same parents, and one record is a fragment». It catches nine groups** — *same year and place* falls 8 → 2 and *same year only* 8 → 5. Four Blažević of Mrzli Dol 6, two Kalanj of Klenovica (Lovre/Lovro × Ana Pavelić), three Žubrinić (Philippus × Maria Begović). **Not one of the nine is a plausible sibling pair**: in every case the stub carries no date detail of its own at all.

**Six of the nine have index support.** Ivan, Mile, Marko and Ane as above; **Andreas 1844** and **Magdalena 9 May 1847** each return exactly one baptism, and the 1847 entry's parents — *Philippus Žubrinich × Maria Begovich* — match one of the two tree records to the letter.

**It is ranked below the same-day tiers and it is not a confirmation.** Two siblings can share a birth year and two parents, and a year without a day cannot rule that out — which is why the tier is named for what it observes rather than for what it concludes. **It is on [/duplicates](/duplicates/)**, because a tier the reader cannot see is worse than no tier at all.

**And a veto the tool was missing, which is the same idea the other way round.** It had *«rejected — two death years»* — a necronym is two children, because **one person dies once**. **It had nothing for births.**

**Magdalena Kalanj** was being carried as a live duplicate: **8 June 1829 at Klenovica** in one record, **19 February 1829 at Ledenice** in the other. A different day, a different month and a different village — and the only reason she sat in *«same year only»* rather than in the rejections is that the tool never looked at whether two birth days could both be true.

**«rejected — two birth days» now does, and it is the stronger half**: not two death *years* but two birth *days*, both written out in full and both unhedged. **It fires once.** A group reaches it only when **every** record carries a full date, so a complete copy paired with a year-only stub is untouched — that is the fragment tier's business, not this one.

**Live groups 32 → 31; rejections 28 → 29.** Both vetoes are named on [/duplicates](/duplicates/) with what they mean, because *«rejected» means the evidence for a duplicate failed, not that two people are proved distinct* — and these two are the exception: they are positive evidence of two people.

---

**21 September 2026 — the seven weakest groups were taken by hand, and two of them turned into vetoes the tool can apply itself.**

Of **31 live groups**, twenty-four sit in tiers that already confirm them. The residue was **seven**, in the tiers that say least: *same year only*, *same year and place*, *same day*. Every one was read out in full — parents, spouses, children, places — and two were decidable.

**`rejected — different parents by surname`.** `parent_surnames()` has existed since 15 September and was used **only to withhold confirmation**. That left the very case it was written for sitting in limbo: the two **Alexander Žubrinić** of 14 March 1839 have a Michael for a father in both and mothers reducing to *magdalena* — one **Orešković**, one **Draženović** — so `parents_agree()` correctly refused to call them one boy, and **nothing then called them two.** The group stayed «live», which is the tool saying *I do not know* about something this row had already decided in writing. **A disagreement good enough to withhold a confirmation is good enough to reject.**

**`rejected — one died a child and the other married`.** **Thomas Žubrinić, born 1822**: one record dies in **1829**, aged seven, with no spouse and no children; the other has a wife, **Joanna**, and a son, **Nicolaus**. Those are two people, and **no amount of name-matching says so** — the parents veto needs parents and neither record here has both. What separates them is a life that ended before the other one's began.

**Each new veto fires exactly once across the whole tree**, which is the property that matters: a veto that over-fires hides a real duplicate. The confirming tiers are untouched at 24. **Live 31 → 29.**

## The five that stay live, and why that is the right answer

**Three are one person split down the middle** — the shape this row already named as «the plainest of all» for Danijel Kalanj, where one copy carries the parents and the other the marriage. **Magdalena Žubrinić 1812** (parents *Antonius × Maria* in one, husband *Wolfgangus Adamić* and three children in the other), **Marija Kalanj 1857** (parents *Ivan Kalanj × Josipa Miletić* in one, husband *Tomo Miletić* in the other), **Michael Žubrinić 1802** (father *Jure* and a wife *Helena* in one, a wife *Margarita* and three children in the other). **Nothing contradicts, and nothing confirms**: Danijel was settled by a shared death date and none of these three has one. **They stay live honestly.**

**Two turn on a second marriage.** **Joso Blažević 1843** has *the same parents in both copies* and two different wives, Kate Šojat and Ruže Prpić; **Josip Prpić 1880** has a mother in one copy and both parents in the other, compatible. A man who remarried and a pair of brothers who shared a name are **both ordinary in these villages**, and this archive has met the second often enough — the seven Michaels, the two Georgius Urode — not to guess. **A register settles it and a tier cannot.**

rows.what: The by-name sweep, re-run wide — one new pair, one false friend, one lead
rows.note:
The by-name file was built out of **Selce and its neighbours**, where the connectors are *aliter · dictus · dicti* and the scribe **underlines** the pair. Karlobag, found on 15 September, uses ***vulgò*** and does **not** underline. So the sweep that produced 17 phrases **was looking for the wrong shape in every parish except one**. Re-run it across the pages already read with the connector list widened — *vulgò · alias · rečeni · zvani* — and against the surnames the tree carries as double-barrelled, which is where a by-name hides once it has been absorbed (ahnentafel 106 «Smojver Vukić» was exactly that).

---

**Re-run 15 September 2026 across every transcription on disk** — `readings.psv`, `found.psv`, `searched.json`, all of `notes/`, the film maps and the grave surveys — with the connector list widened to *aliter · alias · dictus · dicti · dicta · vulgò · rečeni · zvani · vide · ut ibi · cognomine · nuncupatus*. **123 connector phrases in 54 files.**

**Almost all of them were already in the file**, which is the answer the row wanted: the narrow sweep had not in fact missed a parish, because the Karlobag *vulgò* pairs were caught by hand the same day they were read. **Three things came out of it.**

**One new pair.** «*Verbanovich Margarita … **vide** Urbanovich … 15 9bris*» — **Verbanović ⟷ Urbanović**, on the same KAZALO page as «*Vukich vide Smojver*». It had been recorded in the film map and in the register and **never added to the by-name list**, which is exactly the gap a sweep exists to close.

**One false friend, and it matters more than the pair.** In the Otočac ***status animarum***, «*dictus / dicti*» is **not a connector at all** — it is the Latin for *«of the aforesaid»*. «*Michael filius dictus Georgij*» is Michael **son of the said George**; «*Marcus et Josephus … Georgii dicti Gemelli*» is **the twins of the said George**, not a household called Gemelli. **A sweep that harvests every *dicti* invents by-names out of pronouns.** The test — *does the word sit between two names* — is now written at the top of `bynames.psv` so the next sweep does not have to rediscover it.

**And one lead that cannot be closed from disk.** The Karlobag marriages of **1806, folio 3**, list a groom as «*Vulgo Zalic*» — a *vulgò* with **the surname it attaches to missing from the summary table**. It needs that page reopened, not another sweep.

**Still not in the list, and correctly so:** «*Georgius Saldatich aliter Venesarich*» and «*Catharina Polich aliter Antich*», both on image 304 of the Selce deaths. They were read at **half scale** and reading is reading.

rows.what: Audit the film numbers in holdings.psv — and the answer is that the catalogue counts items, not films
rows.note:
**Done in nineteen HTTP calls, 15 September 2026, and the answer is better than the audit this row planned.** The row was going to open every film and guess. It did not need to: `/service/search/catalog/item/koha:<n>` returns one `film_note` entry **per ITEM**, each with its `digital_film_no`, its **physical roll number** and its **item range**. Nineteen calls, eighty-two films, written verbatim to **`sources/familysearch/filmnotes.psv`** and checked against a second fetch by SHA-256 before being committed.

**«A film number is not a book» is now explained, not just observed.** The catalogue's unit is the *item*; the viewer's unit is the *roll*. A roll carries several items and **the items on one roll need not come from one parish**.

> **Karlobag's baptisms 1691–1804 are DGS 5481648 — *items 4 to 5 of roll 1419107*. Items 1 to 3 of that same roll are the parish of KAPTOL**, `koha:655210`, three hundred kilometres inland. So `/search/film/005481648` opens the roll at item 1 and lands in Kaptol. That is exactly what happened here, and it cost a sitting.

**Thirty-one of the eighty-two films do not begin at item 1**, across **seventeen of the nineteen parishes**. Trsat's oldest register is *item 8*. Bribir's is *item 7*. Those are the films a DGS number cannot reach, and they must be opened by waypoint.

**The same shape explains Otočac.** DGS 5482656 is *item 6* of roll 1536689 — five items of something else come first — and 5482657 is catalogued as births *and* deaths because it is *items 1–2*, two books, which is why walking it gives 483 images of baptisms and then END OF ROLL.

**And a book can have two film numbers.** Ledenice's registers were filmed twice: roll 1419155 (DGS 5482218) and roll 2119536 (DGS 5498069) are **the same three books**, decades apart. Neither is wrong. `holdings.psv` had only the first.

**One real gap closed.** Brinje sat in `holdings.psv` as *«film notes not pulled»* with no DGS number at all — and nothing noticed, because nothing compared the file with its source. It is **DGS 5498262** (Rođeni 1888-1900, Vjenčani 1888-1899) and **5498263** (Umrli 1888-1899). That is [row 50](/worklist/) answered as a side effect. **`tools/holdingscheck.py` now gates the build** so the summary can never again claim a year the catalogue does not have.

rows.what: Which parishes the record index covers, and for which events — answered
rows.note:
**Answered 15 September 2026, and it re-orders the rows above it.** Eight surnames of this family were swept through the index and tallied by place and event type; the result is in `sources/familysearch/index-coverage.psv`.

**Indexed for baptisms only — these are walks, not lookups:** **Otočac** (165 baptisms, not one death), **Selce** (77, confirmed twice), **Karlobag** (four surnames tested, every hit a baptism, range 1717–1861), **Krmpote-Vodice**.

**Deaths are indexed:** **Senj** — also under the Latin place string ***Senia***, which a search for «Senj» misses — **Krivi Put**, **Novi Vinodolski**, and thinly **Crikvenica**.

**This corrected row 23 before it was started.** That row was written asserting the Karlobag death index reached ten ancestors; the earlier evidence for that was a Karlobag date range of 1717–1861 which turns out to be **entirely baptisms**. Row 23 is a walk through the book's own KAZALO, not an index lookup — and the KAZALO is ordered **by folio, not alphabetically**, so a surname is found by scanning, not by jumping to a letter.

**And a trap worth more than the map.** Ahnentafel 27 is indexed under **Pilipić**, her married name — a search for *Uroda* returns nothing at Senj. **A married woman's death is indexed under her husband's surname.** Every sweep for a maiden name will walk past her.

rows.what: The twenty-five unplaced villages — twenty-two were never villages, and three are
rows.note:
`targets.json` carries **25 unplacedVillages** — place strings from the tree that no parish in `parishes.psv` claims. Each one is either a spelling the gazetteer does not fold, a village in a parish not yet in the table (which is how **Bribir** and **Sv. Juraj** were added on 14 September), or a place outside this family's districts. Until they are placed, the people standing on them cannot be routed to a book.

---

**Triaged 15 September 2026, and the list is mostly not what it looked like.**

**Eleven are emigration destinations** — Port Pirie, Quorn, Port Germein, Whyalla, Yarraville, Marrickville, Sydney, Kurri Kurri, Arizona, Johannesburg, and «South Australia» itself. **Nine are cities and regions outside these districts** — Zagreb, Osijek, Pula, Belgrade, Garešnica, Fužine, Sveti Križ, Tomašica, «Yugoslavia». No parish table should claim any of them and none is a defect.

**Two were data artefacts and are fixed at the tool.**

* «**"Croatia, Church Books, 1516-1994, " database with images…**» was the *birthplace* of three people — **a source citation pasted into a place field**. A gazetteer that parses it invents a village. `parishlib` now recognises a citation and returns **no place**, which is the truth.
* «**Montani  Stanište**» with two spaces was a different village from «Montani Stanište» with one, so **ahnentafel 111 and her own father stood in two places that are one place**. `norm()` now collapses internal whitespace.

**And three are real Croatian places, behind four direct ancestors.**

| Place | Who stands on it |
|---|---|
| **Smiljan**, Općina Gospić | **ahnentafel 426**, Simoni Pekass |
| **Montani Stanište** | **ahnentafel 111**, Lucia Tomljanović, and **ahnentafel 222**, her father Pauli |

**Those are not gaps in the record. They are gaps in the gazetteer**, and the difference now shows: see [row 45](/worklist/) and **[row 56](/worklist/)**, which carries the job of establishing which parish each belongs to.

rows.what: The walls were re-graded — one had stopped being a wall, and the tool could not see it
rows.note:
**Done, 15 September 2026, and the answer was not the one this row expected.** The walls are drawn on [our line](/tree/). `walls.json` was **byte-identical at every commit this week** — 9 unplaced, 7 nameless, 6 outside, 4 reachable — while **nine direct ancestors were read**. That looked like a correct null and was not.

**`walls.py` could not see the reading.** It loads `ancestors.json` and `placefixes.json` and nothing else: the parish table tells it what is **filmed**, and nothing told it what had been **read**. So it printed «*This wall is reachable and **has not been opened***» on four walls, and for three of them the register had been opened by this archive that same morning.

**And one wall was false.** Ahnentafel **220, Nicolaus Gerkacs**, read «*No place is recorded for this household anywhere on the line, so there is no register to open. **The wall here is a place, not a name.***» His death entry puts him **in his son Antonius's house at Karlobag**. The tree has no birthplace for him; a document does.

**Both fixed at the tool.** `walls.py` now reads `sources/readings.psv` and says which documents are held and **which book is still shut**. `sources/walls.psv` is created with a format — `ahn|field|value` — where **`place`** supplies a place read off a document and **`why`** cites it; a place does *not* assert a grade, it is fed back through the normal grading so the kind stays derived.

**Ahnentafel 220 moves *unplaced* → *reachable*. 8 unplaced now, 5 reachable.**

**And the re-grade names the next job.** Ahnentafel **104, 108, 212 and 220** all want the same book — **Karlobag baptisms, 1691–1861, filmed, and nobody has opened it for any of them.** Four walls, one sitting, and it is the highest-yield unopened book on the chart.

rows.what: The stones are matched against the right pool at last — and the sixth blind tool was the one file written to stop it
rows.note:
**The first job is done, 15 September 2026: `sources/graves/*.psv` is wired in and published at [/stones/](/stones/).** `tools/graves.py` now reads the photographed surveys beside the Find a Grave harvest and **keeps the two kinds of evidence apart by construction** — every top-level key of `graves.json` still counts the **index** and nothing else, so [Port Pirie](/port-pirie/)'s «*72 memorials and not one of them is in Croatia*» stays true. The surveys live under `stones`.

**226 names, 137 of them `r`.** Otočac 32, Senj 194. **16 match a person here** and **66 stones carry more than one name**, which is the same household claim a plot number makes.

**Two things the wiring taught that the files alone did not.**

* **A Croatian stone gives a married woman under her husband's surname.** Matching on the maiden name alone missed ahnentafel 3, 5 and 7 outright. The matcher now tries `rel.spouses` too, and marks those matches as made through a marriage. That is three direct ancestors recovered by one rule.
* **The ±1 birth-year drift is not a Senj quirk and it does not run one way.** Putting the disagreements side by side surfaced a third — **Franjo Žubrinić at Otočac, 1846 on the stone for 1845 in the tree** — and showed that an earlier note's claim that the stones were *consistently* a year early was **wrong**. Ljubomir's is early; the other two are late. Corrected in the note, the register and the page. **Three disagreements, all births, all one year, against not one death year in dispute in 226 names.**

**The matcher reuses the archive's own vocabulary** — `givennames.json` already knew that Stjepan is Stephannes and that **Franjo is not Franciska**, which is what stopped the first draft joining a man to a woman. Only an **`r`** row may contradict the tree: a `p` digit is not evidence and has been wrong four times.

**What is left is the original second job.** **56 of the 72 Find a Grave memorials still match nobody**, and **210 of the 226 stone names** likewise. Some are collateral lines, some are the *found* people of [row 47](/worklist/), some are strangers. The house numbers from row 1 give a handle at Otočac; at Senj the surnames are this family's — Prpić, Špalj, Papić, Vukelić, Tomljanović, Boras.

---

**The matcher was reading the register file, not the tree — and it was the fifth tool in this archive caught doing it.**

`graves.py` matched stones against **`people.json` and nothing else**. That is not the tree, and it is not even everyone with a page: **fifty-two direct ancestors sit in `ancestors.json` and not in it**, so their graves could not match by construction. Beyond both is everyone who exists only as a name on somebody else's record — a parent, a spouse, a child — **with no page and no slug**.

**Sixteen matches became twenty-one, and every new one is a person with no page.** Martin, Lucija and Kata Špalj; Nikola Šojat; and **Ivan Defrančeski, 1925–1995, Hedviga's husband** — who now matches his own gravestone **because the matcher was taught where to look**, not because somebody wrote a correction by hand. That is the difference between fixing an instance and fixing a tool, and this archive had been doing the first.

**One person turned out to be claimed by two stones.** Two Senj stones read **KATA ŠPALJ** — *1884–1975* and *1886–1981* — and the tree holds exactly **one** Kate Špalj, born 1886, with **no death recorded**. Both matched her, because a match needs a year within two and there was no death year to disagree with. **The better-scoring stone keeps the match, the other is unmatched again, a tie drops both, and the contest is published either way.** One of those two women is not in this tree, and publishing her under somebody else's name would be the Defrančeski mistake run backwards: **not a person missed, a person invented.**

**What is left is what was always left**: 56 Find a Grave memorials and 205 stone names matching nobody. The pool they are matched against is now the right pool, which is the precondition for the rest.

---

**20 September 2026 — and it happened a sixth time, to the file written to prevent it.**

`tools/graves.py` was taught on 15 September to match against the tree rather than the register file, and the note above calls that *the fifth tool in this archive caught doing it*. It was still not the right pool. **`sources/found.psv` was not in it** — and that file exists for one reason: a person who is in a register and **not in the tree** had nowhere to be recorded. It holds the single population a stone is most likely to name and the tree least likely to explain.

**The cost was one name, and it is the name that proves the point.** «**MATILDA PAPIĆ 1895–1921**» stands third on a Senj cross. She was photographed, **read at full resolution**, found to be absent from the tree, and **written down in `found.psv` as a discovery** — the archive's own record of its own finding. Then the matcher ran and reported her stone as matching nobody, because *the file written to hold her was not the file she was matched against*. **Both her years agree to the digit.**

**Matched stone names 21 → 22, and nothing else moved** — the other six found people who share a surname with an unmatched stone are Žubrinići at Otočac, and not one of them agrees on a given name or a year. The pass is conservative and stayed conservative.

**She keeps her null slug, and the page now says what she is.** The row would otherwise have printed «*in the tree, with no page of their own*», which is the one thing she is not. A found person stands **beside** the tree — that separation is what `found.psv` is for, and a matcher that quietly dissolved it would have been worse than one that could not see her.

**What is still left is what was always left**, and it is not a matching problem: **204 stone names and 56 memorials match nobody** because this archive does not hold those people. The surnames are the family's — 45 Prpić, 21 Papić, 20 Žubrinić, 19 Špalj, 18 Vukelić — so they are collateral lines and strangers, and only a register separates the two.

rows.what: Four of the found people were in the tree — and one of them is Hedviga's husband
rows.note:
**Done, 15 September 2026, and it caught the thing it was written to catch.** The row said each of the found people needed re-testing **against parent and spouse references, not just published names**, because this archive had already been wrong that way once. It was wrong that way again, and worse.

**Four rows came out of `found.psv`.**

* **Thomas Žubrinić, 1846** — published, and both parents match: Michael Žubrinić × Helena Orešković.
* **Luce Žubrinić, 1850** — published, both parents match: Mio × Jele Orešković.
* **Helena Orešković** — in the tree as a **parent reference with no page of her own**, which is precisely the Karlobag-wives case repeating.
* **IVAN DEFRANČESKI, 1925–1995** — recorded from [the Senj gravestone](/stones/) as *«the surname does not occur once in this archive's tree»*. **He is Hedviga's husband.** The tree carries *Ivan Anton Defrančeski, b. 1925 d. 1995*, on her own marriage, with a **null slug** because he is not published — so a search of `people.json` returns nothing. Both dates match the stone exactly. **The archive photographed the grave of the man at its centre and filed him as a stranger for a day.**

**The lesson was already written down and did not stop it happening**, so it is a gate now. **`tools/foundcheck.py`** tests every `found.psv` row against **every name in the tree** — published people and every `rel.parents`, `rel.spouses`, `rel.siblings` and `rel.children` reference — two ways: *name + year within one*, and *name + BOTH parents agreeing*. A match a person has looked at and dismissed goes in a `SETTLED` table **with the reason**; anything else **fails the build**. It runs as `check:found`.

**Eighteen people remain in `found.psv`** — the number this row started with, arrived at honestly. Three still resemble somebody in the tree and all three are settled in writing: *Maria Rosaria Antić* (ahnentafel 24 has no children published at all), *Maria Magdalena Theresia* and *Maria Žubrinić* (the parents fail the test), and **Matilda Papić, who probably IS Franka or Sulka** — the open question [row 53](/worklist/) left standing, not an error.

rows.what: Two emigration threads with no route in
rows.note:
Both are in the register as *pending* and neither can move without a decision that is not this archive's to make. **FindMyPast — Port Pirie electoral rolls**: eleven of nineteen read, and the trial expired before the rest; the rolls give an address and an occupation year by year, which is how a household is watched over time. **Southern Rhodesian immigration 1953–65**: an entire country known from two words on a later record, and **no route into it has been identified at all** — which is a different thing from having searched and found nothing. Both want either a subscription or a decision to let them stand as honest nulls.

---

**21 September 2026 — the electoral-roll half of this row is CLOSED, and has been for days without the row saying so.** It reads «eleven of nineteen read, and the trial expired before the rest». **The month's subscription finished them**: `sources/findmypast/electoral-rolls-2026-09-16.psv` holds **fifty transcripts for nineteen people** across **five roll years** — 1913 and 1935 in New South Wales, 1939, 1941 and 1943 in South Australia — each with an address, an occupation and the household at that address.

**They are published**, with the rest of the catch, at [the Catch Abroad](/abroad/). **What this row wanted — a household watched over time — is exactly what an address repeated across roll years gives**, and the page marks how many do.

**The Southern Rhodesian half is untouched and still has no route in**, which is why this row stays open rather than closing. Splitting the two would have made that visible sooner; a row with two threads reports the state of whichever one somebody last wrote about.

rows.what: The five letters, and where each one stands
rows.note:
**Added 15 September 2026 because the set was not visible.** Four of the five letters had rows here — 10, 11, 12 and 13 — and **the fifth had none**, which is the one that generated the other three. A reader of this list would have counted four letters.

**Državni arhiv u Rijeci, Ispostava u Senju** — sent **13 September**, answered **14 September** by **Denis Rukavina**: «*Sabirni centar u Senju nema u svom posjedu arhivsku građu kojom bi se moglo udovoljiti Vašem zahtjevu*» — the Senj collection centre does not hold it — and he **named three doors in its place**: Rijeka, Gospić, and the competent parish offices. **That reply is why rows 10, 11 and 12 exist.** It was a nil return that did more work than most positive ones.

| To | Sent | Where it stands |
|---|---|---|
| DAR, Ispostava u Senju | 13 Sep | **Answered 14 Sep** — nil return, named three further doors |
| Državni arhiv u Gospiću | 13 Sep | **Acknowledged 14 Sep**, queued — [row 13](/worklist/) |
| Državni arhiv u Rijeci | 15 Sep | **Answered 15 Sep**, refused — [row 10](/worklist/) |
| Župni ured Senj | 15 Sep | no reply — [row 11](/worklist/) |
| Župa Krmpote, via Ledenice | 15 Sep | **Answered 15 Sep** — the registers left the parish — [row 12](/worklist/) |

**Three of the three doors Senj named have now been tried, and four of the five letters have answers.** Only the **Župni ured Senj** is still out.

**And the reasoning that produced these letters has been half disproved.** It was written here that *«if anything comes, it is most likely to come from a parish priest, because the books the films do not cover are the ones that never left parish custody»*. Krmpote answered the same day: **its registers went to the Rijeka Archdiocese, and from there to the State Archive.** The parish has no contact with its own older books. That is worth leaving on the record as written and then corrected, because it is the assumption that shaped where five letters went.

Full text of every reply is in `requests/REPLIES.md`; the letters as sent are in `requests/sent/`.

rows.what: Brinje — never opened, and not in this archive's gazetteer
rows.note:
**Found by the missing-row gate on 15 September 2026.** It had been *pending* in the register since the 14th and had no row here at all.

**Not one page of the Brinje register has ever been opened**, and Brinje is **not in this archive's gazetteer**. It got onto the list the hard way: a 1910 American manifest gave a Kalanj's residence as *Brinje*, which sent someone back to re-read a Latin baptism of 1864 — ***«Brinjensis parochiae ruricolae»***, country people of the parish of Brinje, **forty kilometres inland** from the coast where this archive had always put them.

Three surnames meet there — **Kalanj, Perković and Borić**. The films are catalogue-verified for **1888–1900** across births, marriages and deaths, which is late for an 1864 baptism but right for the generation that emigrated. The Gospić letter also asks for the **Kalanj × Perković marriage** at Brinje, so [row 13](/worklist/) and this row may answer each other.

**The films are located, 15 September 2026.** [Row 42](/worklist/)'s catalogue sweep pulled the film notes Brinje was missing: **DGS 5498262** — *Rođeni 1888-1900, Vjenčani 1888-1899*, items 1–4 of roll 2121763 — and **DGS 5498263** — *Umrli 1888-1899*, item 1 of roll 2121764. Both begin at item 1, so **both are reachable by film number**, which is not true of thirty-one of this archive's eighty-two films.

**The dates are the problem and they always were.** 1888 is twenty-four years after the baptism that sent us here, *«Brinjensis parochiae ruricolae»* of 1864. What these two films can carry is the **Kalanj × Perković marriage** the Gospić letter asks for, if it falls 1888-1899, and the generation that emigrated. **Brinje is still not in the gazetteer** and still has not been opened.

---

**20 September 2026 — which books are indexed is now measured rather than assumed.** `sources/familysearch/indexed.psv` holds the table, probed parish by parish through the persona search API. **And the first version of that table was wrong, corrected the same day: marriages and deaths ARE indexed**, through *Hungary, Croatia-Slavonia, Marriages 1678–1927* and *…Deaths 1681–1990*. They were invisible because **the search is ranked and capped** — a broad query returns about sixty rows and whole collections sit below the cut. **Narrow by date and they appear.** **Brinje has nothing indexed**, under Kalanj or Marić, for any event. Combined with [row 57](/worklist/)'s finding that **no Kalanj from Klenovica or Brinje filed a US naturalisation petition**, this village is reachable only by opening its film — which is what this row said, and it is now measured from both directions.

rows.what: Ahnentafel 11 — the emptiest person on the direct line
rows.note:
**Found by the missing-row gate on 15 September 2026**, and it is the row that proved the gate should have no exemptions — it was written off as «a plan» when it is a list of documents sitting in a book this archive has already opened.

**«Ana Shambul Marić» is a name, two tree links and nothing else.** Her father is a **surname with no given name**; her mother is **not in the tree at all**.

**The name is probably not her name.** She is carried as *«Ana Shambul Marić»* and elsewhere *«rođen Shumbul Marić»*, and this archive has met that shape before — the **nadimak** written beside the surname, *Antich Papa*, *Jellichich dictis Jurešina*. If **Šumbul** is the house name then the surname to search is **Marić**, and the by-name is the only thing separating this family from every other Marić in Lika. *A hypothesis, deliberately kept out of the by-names data, which holds only phrases read off a page* — and note that [row 41](/worklist/) has since widened the connector list, which may bear on it.

**What is reachable, and it is cheap.** The couple's children are Lucca (1853), Marija (about 15 September 1858), Jacobus and Tereza (1867). **Otočac births are filmed 1834–1858**, so **Lucca's and Marija's baptisms are both inside the book** — the same book as [row 27](/worklist/), which is index-led. Do them together.

---

**The hypothesis is now supported from inside the tree, 15 September 2026, and it did not need a book.** Written up in [notes/ana-sumbul-maric.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/ana-sumbul-maric.md); four things the GEDCOM says on its own.

* **«Shambul» is in the SURNAME field and the given name is empty** — the record is literally `1 NAME  /Shambul Marić/`. So this was never *a man called Shambul whose surname was Marić*. The whole string arrived as a surname.
* **His other two children are plain Marić.** Mathias and Joannes, same father, same family record, no second word. **A surname does not attach to one child of three. A by-name does** — it follows a household, a house or a man, and the priest writes it when he needs to tell one Marić from another.
* **The two sources disagree, and neither is a document.** A MyHeritage Smart Match (QUAY 3) whose URL reads *shumbul*, and a Geni world tree (QUAY 4) reading *shambul*. **Šumbul in one, Shambul in the other**, and both are other people's trees.
* **Her married name is recorded separately** — `_MARNM Žubrinić` — so the tree already keeps apart the name she was born with and the name she was buried under, which is the distinction the Senj stones forced on the grave matcher the same day.

**So the surname to search is Marić**, with Šumbul as the discriminator — the way *Papa* separates one Papić household at Selce and *Smojver* one Vukić at Karlobag. **It stays out of `sources/bynames.psv`**, which holds only phrases read off a page; this one was read off a URL, and the file it is in says so.

**What is left is the book, and it is the one row 27 wants.** Otočac births are filmed 1834–1858 and **Lucca's (1853) and Marija's (about 15 September 1858) baptisms are both inside it**. Two entries would give her father's given name, her mother's existence, and whether the priest wrote Šumbul beside Marić.

---

**20 September 2026 — searched the moment FamilySearch came back, and the answer is that this row is out of date about its own person.**

The Otočac index gives **«Maria Zubrinić, 15 September 1858, of Nicolaus Zubrinić and Anna Marić»** — ahnentafel 10 and 11 named together. Against a row that opens *«Ana Shambul Marić is a name, two tree links and nothing else»*, that looked like the row falling.

**It is the same entry `sources/readings.psv` has held since 14 September, and the reading already here is better than the index**, because it carries the household the index drops: *«Rustica e Šumećica N° 2»*. **And there is a second**, the Otočac baptism of **3 July 1856**, same house, naming her **«Anna nata Štrumbulko»** — **the by-name attested in a register**, which is what [the plan note](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/ana-maric-plan.md) had as a hypothesis.

**So she was never empty, and this row's opening sentence has been wrong since the 14th.** Recorded rather than quietly fixed, because the archive announced a rediscovery once before with the Karlobag index and the habit is worth catching every time.

**What the index actually adds is one citation and two negatives.**

* The 1858 reading had no ARK. It has one: `1:1:QKMK-3MZV`.
* **Her own baptism is not indexed, and the reason is coverage.** A control search returns **three** Marić entries at Otočac in total — 1844, 1844 and 1852 — and she was born about **1836**. The film is still the only route to her own entry, and to **ahnentafel 22's given name**, which no baptism of her child will ever supply.
* **«Shambul» is a real surname 250 km away.** Every *Shambula* in the index is at **Donji Mosti** or **Zrinski Topolovac** in Bjelovar-Križevci, or **Bartolovec** near Varaždin — Hungarian country, nothing to do with the Lika coast. **Not one is in Lika-Senj.** That is negative evidence for the *nadimak* reading, and a warning: a searcher who takes the surname at face value lands among real people in the wrong county.

---

**20 September 2026 — the by-name hypothesis now has evidence from OUTSIDE the file it is trying to correct, and it is a counting argument.**

Everything supporting «Šumbul is a *nadimak*» was, until today, **internal to the GEDCOM**: the string sits in the surname field, only one of three siblings carries it, the two sources disagree about its spelling. Good reasoning about a file. **Searched across the whole Croatian record index:**

| form | exact hits in all of Croatia |
|---|---|
| **Štrumbulko** | **1** — and it is ours |
| **Shambul**, the tree's own spelling | **0** |
| Sumbulko, Strumbul, Sumbulic | **0** |
| Sumbul | 7 — **all Dalmatian**, all with Italian given names |

**Marić, for contrast, is ordinary at Otočac** — seven in a single page for births 1800–1880. **A surname leaves a trail of cousins; this one leaves a single entry.** And the seven *Sumbul* records are three hundred kilometres away in the wrong language. **In the index, «Shambul» is not a surname anywhere.**

**And the index shows the alternation itself**, which the film had already shown:

    3 July 1856       Stephanus Bubrinić  ·  Nicolaus Bubrinić × Anna ŠTRUMBULKO  ·  QKMK-SK94
    15 September 1858  Maria Zubrinić     ·  Nicolaus Zubrinić × Anna MARIĆ       ·  QKMK-3MZV

Same father's given name, same parish, two years apart, **the mother's family name different in the two entries**. This archive already held both — `readings.psv` has carried them since the Otočac sitting and annotates the 1856 row «the by-name attested». **What is new is that it is visible in the index, in text, without the film.**

**«Bubrinić» is Žubrinić** — a third surname this index has mangled on this line in one day, beside **«Piberich»** and **«Pillopich»** for Pilipić. The query that returned both entries **named no surname at all**.

**What it does not settle.** Ahnentafel 22 is still a surname with no given name and ahnentafel 23 is still absent from the tree. **The marriage would name both, and it is not in the index** — searched by surname pair, by spouse given names, with and without the parish, 1845–1865. **Nor is Lucca's 1853 baptism.** So the remaining work is still the book, exactly as this row said.

**It stays out of `sources/bynames.psv`**, which holds only phrases read off a page. [notes/strumbulko-occurs-once-in-croatia.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/strumbulko-occurs-once-in-croatia.md)

rows.what: Ured riječke nadbiskupije — the door the Krmpote priest named
rows.note:
**A third kind of holder, and nobody has tried it.** Not a state archive and not a parish: the **Archdiocesan Office at Rijeka**. vlč. Jakov Filipović, who administers Sv. Jakov Krmpote from Ledenice, says the registers of **every parish he administers** went to the **Riječka Nadbiskupija**, and that as far as he knows the Archdiocese passed them to the **State Archive**.

**What makes it worth a letter rather than a shrug.** The State Archive at Rijeka answered on the same day that it does not do research of this complexity — and **never said what it holds** ([row 10](/worklist/)). The priest says the books are in its care. So **one question is now asked from two directions and answered from neither**: *does the Rijeka baptismal register covering 1 March 1892, and the Sv. Jakov Krmpote register before 1879, survive, and who holds them?*

**That is a holdings question, not a research request** — which matters, because a holdings question is exactly what Rijeka's refusal did not cover, and exactly what an archdiocesan chancery can answer from its own transfer records.

**Owner is David** because sending is his call. The draft can be written here on request; the three asks are the ones already refined in `requests/sent/EMAIL-zupa-krmpote.txt` and `EMAIL-rijeka.txt`, which now need only re-addressing and a covering paragraph explaining who sent us.

rows.what: The Senj «p» rows are read — four dates corrected, and a Žubrinić stone nobody had seen
rows.note:
**Done, 15 September 2026.** Every `p` row in `sources/graves/senj-2024-10-09.psv` was opened again at full resolution. **108 of 194 rows are now `r`**, up from about 60.

**The method that made it practical:** crop to the inscription and resample to about **1,800 px on the long side** — the reader's own display resolution. Enlarging past that is thrown away in the downsample, which is why the first attempts at 4–8× full-frame gained nothing.

**Four readings were wrong and every one was a date off a contact sheet** — Mile Prpić **1985 → 1982**, Karlo Papić-Glavičić **1928 → 1922**, Budimir Boras **1950 → 1954**, and «Pavo» Boras who is ***Fabo***. Two more had **no readable death year at all**; those years ran off the edge of the frame and were guesses, and they are `19??` now. **Nothing in the ancestor block moved** — all twelve direct-line and sibling rows were read at 3–8× the first time and every one was confirmed. The errors fell exactly where the confidence letter said they would, which is the case for keeping it.

**And the pass found a stone the first sweep missed entirely.** Enlarging IMG_8159 for the Gržin inscription brought up the grave behind it: «*IVICA ŽUBRINIĆ 1887–1934 · FANA ŽUBRINIĆ 1890–1974 · MARIJAN ŽUBRINIĆ 1919–1996*». **Žubrinić is ahnentafel 5's maiden surname.** A Žubrinić grave in the town she married into and is buried in is a thread nobody has pulled.

**What is left is not another pass at the same files.** 61 rows stay `p` and 25 stay `?` because the photographs do not contain the digits — steep angles run the line out of frame, flowers stand on the dates. Those rows, and **IMG_8071**'s fallen «MARIJAN …» under the reeds, want ten minutes in the cemetery.

rows.what: Karlobag baptisms — the book does not need opening; it is indexed
rows.note:
The re-grade of [row 45](/worklist/) ended by naming its own successor. **Four of the five «reachable» walls want one book**: Karlobag baptisms, **1691–1861**, filmed as DGS **5481648**, and nobody has opened it for any of them.

| Ahn | Who | Baptism to look for |
|---|---|---|
| **104** | Jacob Pilipić, *captain of the port* | about **1741** |
| **108** | Georgi Uroda | about **1750** |
| **212** | Josiph Smojver Vukić | **1731** |
| **220** | Nicolaus Gerkacs | **1717** |

**All four are inside the filmed range**, and a baptism is the one document that names both parents — which is exactly what a wall is short of. **Four walls could fall in one sitting.**

**It is not a cold start.** The film is the archive's best-mapped: [row 23](/worklist/) measured the deaths volume's folio anchors and its KAZALO letter positions, and `sources/familysearch/film-005481649-karlobag.json` holds the ARKs. The baptisms are a **different film** — 5481648 — and [the Karlobag note](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/karlobag-films.md) warns that its film number does not resolve to one book: the 1771–1804 baptisms sit under waypoint `9RK1-3Y9:391644801,391849401,391849402`. **Check the waypoint before trusting the film number**, and expect the 1691–1770 volume to be a separate one again.

**And look for the by-name.** Two of the four are already known under one — *Smojver **vulgò** Vukić* — and the Karlobag indexes file households under the *nadimak* with a «vide».

---

**Why the film number does not open it, settled 15 September 2026.** Not a quirk and not a bad catalogue entry. **DGS 5481648 is *items 4 to 5* of physical roll 1419107, and items 1 to 3 of that roll are the parish of KAPTOL** — `koha:655210`, three hundred kilometres inland. `/search/film/005481648` opens the roll at item 1, so it lands in Kaptol every time. Thirty-one of this archive's eighty-six films are in the same position; [row 42](/worklist/) has the whole table.

**The route in is the waypoint**, `9RK1-3Y9:391644801,391849401,391849402` — **327 images**, «Births (Rođeni) 1691-1770 · Births 1771-1804 · Birth Index (Kazalo rođeni)». Known ARKs inside it: image 217 = `3:1:3QS7-L99C-L998-5` (1781), image 250 = `3:1:3QS7-L99C-L99J-1`, image 310 = `3:1:3QS7-L99C-L99Q-L`. **Image 310 is inside the Kazalo** — a narrow-column index page, checked at contact-sheet scale — so the index is near the end where it should be, and the four baptisms are lookups rather than a walk.

**A fifth wall joined the queue the same day.** [Row 56](/worklist/) put ahnentafel 426, **Simoni Pekass**, at Smiljan — a real parish whose films begin in 1834, which is a century too late for him. His daughter **Antonia married Josiph Smojver Vukić at Karlobag on 20 November 1752**, so **her baptism is in this same volume** and will name him. Five walls, one book.

**What stops it is not FamilySearch.** The Browser pane is hidden in the app, so screenshots cannot composite and a register page cannot be read at full resolution — see [row 21](/worklist/).

---

**17 September 2026: this row was wrong about its own book.** It has stood for days as *«four walls want the same unopened book»*, and a session was spent on how to get a legible page out of a hidden browser pane. **The book does not have to be opened. It is INDEXED, and the index is text.**

**And this archive already knew — which is the part worth writing down.** `found.psv` holds **six children of ahnentafel 108** — Dominicus 1764, Petrus Jacobus 1767, Heva Joanna 1769, Maria Catharina 1772, Anton Joanis 1780, Joannis 1784 — every one citing **«Karlobag births, indexed»**. A previous sitting worked the Uroda household entirely out of the record index, and found.psv also holds **Antonius Gergacs, son of ahnentafel 220**. **This row was written anyway**, naming four other walls in the same parish as waiting on an unopened film. The catalogue confirmed it independently on the 16th — `fs_indexed: "Y"` — read, quoted, filed. **So this is not a discovery. It is a tool the archive had in its hands and applied to one household out of five.**

**A search of *Croatia, Church Books* restricted to Karlobag, 1690–1780, returns baptisms with BOTH PARENTS as searchable text**: Roxanich 1704, 1705, 1707; Bevardich 1742 and 1752; Bovari 1749. **That is the volume, and the four baptisms are lookups in a search box rather than a walk through 327 images.**

**And it produced a household within minutes.** Ahnentafel **426 Simoni Pekass** × **427 Mara Pekass** have **no dates at all** in this archive; their only anchor is that their daughter Antonia married at Karlobag on 20 November 1752. The index has a **Šimun Pekasa at Karlobag**: **Margarita 28 Oct 1719** (father Simon), **Katarina 19 Jun 1734** (Simuna and **Stoja**), **Perina 29 Jun 1738** (Simuna and **MARE**).

**A candidate, not a proof, and the difference matters.** What agrees is a given name, a wife's given name, a parish and a window. **Antonia's own baptism has not been found** — *Antonia Pekas* at Karlobag returns ten records and none is hers. **And there are two wives**: Stoja in 1734, Mare in 1738. Which one Antonia belongs to decides whether ahnentafel 427 is Mara at all.

**It also contradicts [row 56](/worklist/), written yesterday**, which put Simoni Pekass at **Smiljan** on the tree's own place string and ruled him unreachable because Smiljan's films begin in 1834. Both can be true — a man born at Smiljan can marry into Karlobag — but **the reachability verdict changes**, because the Karlobag index reaches 1704.

**And the image route is not wasted, it is demoted.** A chunked, hash-verified transfer out of a hidden pane now works — about **twelve round trips per page**, SHA-256 matching end to end. **Images are for what the index does not carry**: the house number, the *Conditio* column, the by-name beside the surname. Those are still worth the twelve.

---

**One new person, read out of the index and into `found.psv`.** **Margaritha Smojver, baptised 9 July 1764 at Karlobag, entry 270** — *«Entry for Margaritham Smoiver and Josephi Smoiver»*, mother **Antoniæ**, ark `1:1:QKMX-YLY7`. That is a daughter of **ahnentafel 212 × 213** the tree does not have: born twelve years after their marriage of 20 November 1752 and twelve years before Josiph's death in 1776.

**The other two walls resisted, and the reason is spelling.** *Nicolaus Gerkacs* (ahn 220, b.1717) returns nothing at Karlobag in range — the index renders the surname *Gergacs, Gergocz, Geraecs, Gergich*, and the Karlobag Gergacs households it does hold are **Antonio × Francisca** and **Michael × Lucia**, 1777–1789, a generation too late. *Jacob Pilipić* (ahn 104, ~1741) is worse: at Karlobag the index writes him **Pidepics** and **Pilleppics**. **The index inherits every difficulty of the hand it was made from** — it removes the need to find the page, not the need to know how a name was spelled.

---

**Searching by FATHER separates two Šimuns at Karlobag, a lifetime apart.** The early one — **Joseip 1 Mar 1705, Margarita 28 Oct 1719, Katarina 19 Jun 1734 (mother STOJA), Perina 29 Jun 1738 (mother MARE)** — is the household that fits **ahnentafel 426 × 427**, because **Mare is Mara**. The late one is *Simone Pekkas × Maria*, 1783–1795.

**He spans thirty-three years of baptisms and two wives that are not the same woman.** Either Šimun married twice in a long life or there are a father and a son of one name. **Nothing found decides it.**

**And the Antonia the index offers is the wrong Antonia.** *Antonia Pehasa*, baptised **18 January 1742**, parents **Osipa Pehasa and Monde** — she **cannot** be ahnentafel 213, who married in **1752** and bore Vicentius in **1754**: that would make her ten at the wedding and twelve at the birth. **She is in `found.psv` specifically to be ruled out**, because the next reader will meet her first. Her father *Osipa* is Josip — and a **Joseip Pekasu was baptised to Šimun in 1705**, which would make her Šimun's granddaughter.

**So ahnentafel 213 was born between 1719 and 1734, in the gap between Margarita and Katarina, and her baptism is not in the index under any spelling tried.** The index holds four of Šimun's children and evidently not all of them. **For that one entry the image is still the answer**, and the twelve round trips are what it costs.

---

**20 September 2026, with FamilySearch signed in again — and the first thing the index found was a fault in this archive, not in the register.**

**Ahnentafel 428 and 429 were placed at Karlobag three days ago «on the strength of their grandchild's death — the tree's own words about the tree's own people, not a document». There was a document.** `sources/readings.psv` had held it since **10 September**:

> `caetano-bacchi|baptism|1779|…|Karlobag, 12 January 1779 — "ex Angelo et Catharina Bacchi"`

**Their names are in the citation.** The reading was filed under their son and never reached them, so `walls.py` went on printing *«this wall is reachable and has not been opened»* about two people whose names sat in the archive's own file. Confirmed in the index the same day as `1:1:QKMX-BWCR`, where the surname is written **BECHI**.

**The rule existed and no tool had it.** [Question 9b](/open-questions/) has said since the 14th that *«a baptism counts as a reading for the child AND for both parents, because it names all three»*. That was being done **by hand — sixteen times — and missed thirty.** `tools/readingslib.py` holds it now and both tools that grade a person read the file the same way: **20 parents credited** with a document that names them. A derived credit is marked as derived and carries the child it came through, because *«a register names you»* and *«a register is about you»* are different claims.

---

**THE INDEX NAMES THE WRONG MOTHER FOR A DIRECT ANCESTOR, and that is the other half of this row.** Searched at Karlobag, the index gives ahnentafel 106's baptism — 18 January 1754 — as *«Osipa Smoiver × **Marie**»*, with the same father's children by *Antonia* in 1752 and 1764 either side of it. Read from the search box alone that is a conflict on the spine.

**It is not.** The entry was read at full resolution on 10 September and the book is kept in Croatian: ***«Isti dan kerstih vicencia Fabiana sina Ospa y Antonie Smoiver»*** — **son of Osip and Antonia.** The register names Antonia, the tree is right, **and the index is simply wrong.**

This row's whole finding was that the book *is indexed* and need not be opened. That still holds. **The correction is that an index finds the page and the page settles the fact** — the spelling failures it was already known for only hide a person, whereas this one names the wrong woman, legibly, on the direct line. [notes/karlobag-index-is-wrong-about-ahn-106.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/karlobag-index-is-wrong-about-ahn-106.md)

---

**Three more things out of the same sweep.**

* **A candidate for ahnentafel 104 at last** — **«Jakomo Pilipicha, 30 November 1739»**, father **«Jakoma Pilipicha»**. The only Pilipić baptism in the index before 1784, and the spelling that finds it is the Croatian **Pilipicha**, not the *Pidepics* and *Pilleppics* three sittings tried. **Offered as a candidate**: «about 1741» is itself an estimate, and the image would give the mother and the house that the index does not.
* **Two children the tree does not have**, both now in `found.psv`: **Antonü Bechi, 11 September 1780**, a second son of ahnentafel 428 × 429; and **Hevam Uroda, September 1773**, a daughter of ahnentafel 108 × 109 — **the second of that name**, after Heva Joanna of 28 December 1769.
* **The index holds the same entry twice under two arks.** Caetano's 1779 baptism is both `QKMX-BWCR` and `QKMX-BWCT`; Antonü's 1780 is `QKMX-B9R1` and `QKMX-B9TM`. **Two arks, one event** — and anything counting index rows as people, or looking for children born on one day, will read it as two.

---

**And then the query changed, and the index stopped being a way to find a person and became a way to rebuild a household.**

Every earlier sitting searched **by person** — a surname, a given name, a year — which finds somebody you already know enough about. **Searching by PARENTS returns the whole household at once.**

**Ahnentafel 110 × 111, Michael Gerkacs and Lucia Tomljanović — six children, and this archive had one.** Magdalena 1787, **Maria August 1789 (ahnentafel 55)**, a second Magdalena 1792, Catharina 1794, Bartholomæus 1797, Mathias 1801.

* **Ahnentafel 55's own baptism was not here.** The archive held her marriage of 1807 and her death of 1834 and never the entry she was christened on.
* **And it names ahnentafel 111.** Lucia Tomljanović was one of the twenty-four direct ancestors with **no document of any kind**, placed at *Montani Stanište*, which is not a parish and never was. She is named in a register six times. **Twenty-four became twenty-three, and the direct line went from 46 read to 47** — through the parent-credit rule written this morning, which is the second time today it has paid on the spine.

**And the by-name did exactly what this row predicted.** It said *«look for the by-name — the Karlobag indexes file households under the nadimak»*. **They do.** Ahnentafel 106 × 107's children are indexed under **both** names: *Maria Vukich 1776*, *Josephus Franciscus Vukich 1777*, *Anna Oliva Vukics 1785* — and *Smojver* in 1782 and 1788. **A searcher who queries only Smojver finds two of the five.** The proof that it is one couple is the archive's own 1781 reading: *«ex Vincentio, et Oliva Smoyver, **vulgò Vukić**, Conjugibus»*.

**Ten children into `found.psv`**, and ahnentafel 55's baptism into `readings.psv` marked **INDEX ONLY**, because nobody has opened the page and this same indexing has been caught twice today getting a name wrong. [notes/karlobag-households-indexed.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/karlobag-households-indexed.md)

---

**20 September 2026 — a hypothesis this row could have been built on, tested and killed the same hour.** Two surnames showed the same shape in the index at Karlobag: **Pilipić silent 1739–1810**, **Gerkacs silent 1721–1773**. That looked like a hole in the indexing sitting exactly over the generation of this row's four walls — which would have meant the film **does** need opening after all, for precisely the people this row says it does not.

**It is not a hole.** A decade census of Karlobag from 1690 to 1780 returns **100 Karlobag baptisms out of every 100 fetched, in every decade**. The index is dense there. **The gaps were spelling, not coverage.**

**And the fix that follows from it found a household in one query.** Searching *father Jacob × mother Catharina* at Karlobag with **no surname at all** returned ahnentafel 52's baptism of 11 March 1768 and three brothers — filed by the index as **Piberich, Pillopich and Pillepich**. See [row 26](/worklist/).

**So this row's thesis survives, with its reason sharpened.** The book need not be opened because it is indexed — but a surname query is the wrong instrument for a book whose hand the indexer could not read. **Query the given names and the parish, and let the surname fall out.**

**Ahnentafel 220 and 110 resisted even that.** *Michael, father Nicolaus, Karlobag, 1757–1767*, surname-free, returns nothing of his; ten spellings of Gerkacs return no Karlobag baptism between 1721 and 1773. **Ahnentafel 221 is still absent from the tree** — Michael has a father and no mother, and his baptism is the entry that would name her.

---

**20 September 2026, later — the surname-free query turned on this row's own walls, and it mostly returned nothing. Which is worth writing down as nothing.**

The method that found ahnentafel 52 under «Piberich» — given names, no surname, a date window, the parish — was put to the four walls and to ahnentafel 105 and 213. **Four clean negatives:**

| Ahn | Query | Result |
|---|---|---|
| **105** | Catharina, father Vicentius, mother Maria, 1724–1730 | **0** |
| **104** | Jacob, 1735–1748 | nothing of his |
| **212** | Josephus, 1728–1735 | nothing of his |
| **220** | Nicolaus, 1713–1721 | nothing of his |

**Ahnentafel 105's own baptism of 30 March 1727 is not in the index under any name at all**, which is a stronger statement than «not under this surname» and settles it: **ahnentafel 210 and 211, Vicentius and Maria Luckinić, cannot be named from the index.** The 1691–1770 film is the only route left to them.

**And the index offers Šimun Pekas a SECOND Antonia, which is also not ahnentafel 213.** «Antonia Pekasovicha, 25 October 1711, father Simuna Pekasovicha», ark `1:1:QKMX-YSF2` — a **sixth** spelling of the surname. She is ruled out on arithmetic: ahnentafel 213 bore Margaritha in 1764 and Joanna in 1770, which this woman would have done at **53 and 59**. She is in `found.psv` beside Antonia Pehasa of 1742 — **the index holds two Antonias to this household, one too old and one too young, and ahnentafel 213 is neither.**

**That narrows her.** Bearing a child in 1770 puts her birth after about 1725; marrying in 1752 puts it before about 1735. **1725–1735**, in the gap between Margarita 1719 and Katarina 1734 — and her baptism is not in the index. **For that one entry the image is still the answer**, exactly as this row said.

rows.what: Twenty-four people with no page had forty-seven unanswered contradictions — all answered
rows.note:
**All forty-seven answered, 15 September 2026, and the gate now fails on them.** `check_site.py` no longer prints a count and carries on: a contradiction about a person with no page fails the build exactly as one about a person with a page does. The bargain `checkcovers` struck — print it until the hole is closed, then close it — is over.

**Not one of the forty-seven needed a register.** The row expected the opposite: it said *do the namesake trap first, it is the one where this archive has an instrument nobody else has*. The instrument is the house number in the *Conditio* column, and it turned out to answer a different question. **Naming which Maria she is needs the book. Showing that the join is wrong only needs the tree's own arithmetic**, and the arithmetic was sitting there the whole time.

**One shape accounts for most of them.** *One spouse slot holding two generations of mothers.* Vladimira Baričević, born **12 December 1907**, is entered as the mother of all fourteen children of a man born 1855 — the eldest of them born 1888. The tell is that **Zdenka Boras is born 12 December 1907 too**: a daughter's birth date copied into the wife's record. Helena Untersinger is the same shape — five children across **thirty-seven years**, the first when she is fourteen and the last eleven years after she is buried. So are both Žubrinić Marias, and Catharina of **Prozor 50**, whose eighth child arrives nineteen years after his father dies.

**The second shape is a sibling recorded as a child.** Marko Butković, born 1872, is the father of Antonija Butković born 1880 — who carries his surname, dies at eleven, and is his sister. Luka Katnić died in **December 1755** and fathers a daughter in 1757 who carries her *mother's* surname: his widow remarried and her second family was hung on her first husband.

**And three were never contradictions at all.** Two are hedged dates — *AFT 1926*, *BEF 1750* — doing exactly what a hedge is for, which `/impossible` already files as «not an error». The third found the only gap in the tool: Marija Šojat's outlying child is **«ABT 1840»**, and the check misses the hedge because it reads the person it is reporting and not the person on the other end of the join.

**A bucket fell out of it.** Joanis Grach's father is entered as *«Grah's for Investigation (not real)»*. This archive audits the tree for sorting buckets and did not have this one: the phrase list was written from the buckets that were causing trouble, so it knew *for sorting* and *to be sorted* and *it seems*, and not **PLACEHOLDER**, **for Investigation** or **(not real)**. Five were missing, parenting **thirty-six people** between them, **none of them published** — which is why nothing on this site was ever wrong, and why nobody noticed. A detector written from the examples in front of it will always be shaped like those examples.

rows.what: Smiljan and Montani Stanište — one is a parish, the other never will be
rows.note:
**Both settled as places, 15 September 2026, and neither settled as a book — which row 45 was right to insist are different questions.**

**Smiljan is its own parish.** `koha:465540`, *Rimokatolička crkva. Župa Smiljan* — not a village of Gospić, which is exactly what this row asked. It is now in `parishes.psv` with its two films. **It does not reach ahnentafel 426.** Smiljan's births are filmed **1834–1857** only, and Simoni Pekass is a generation of about 1700: his daughter Antonia was already marrying in 1752. Gospić was added beside it for one reason — it is the only book in the district that goes back further, and only for **marriages and deaths from 1789**.

**So the way to Simoni Pekass is sideways, and it is a book this archive already wants.** Antonia Pekass married Josiph Smojver Vukić at **Karlobag on 20 November 1752**. Her baptism is inside **Karlobag Rođeni 1691–1770** and will name her father. That is [row 54](/worklist/)'s volume — a fifth wall wanting the same unopened book.

**Montani Stanište is not a parish and the catalogue agrees.** Searched for both *«Stanište»* and *«Montani»*: nothing in Croatia. A *stanište* is a herders' settlement and its events are written into a neighbour's book. **Which neighbour is not established, and no row was invented to pretend otherwise** — `unknown` is a legal value and that is what it carries. What is firm is the daughter: **ahnentafel 111 died 19 September 1809**, inside Karlobag *Umrli 1804–1861*, and that entry would name her father and her house.

**A tool fell over on the way.** `walls.py` accepted a `why` override and then **silently dropped it** unless it arrived with a `place`, because it had only ever been written as the second half of *«a document places them, and here is the document»*. Both sentences above were parsed and thrown away on the first run. A wall can need a sentence without needing to move.

---

**Qualified on 17 September.** This row ruled ahnentafel 426 unreachable because the tree places him at **Smiljan** and Smiljan's films begin in **1834**. The **Karlobag record index reaches 1704**, and it holds a **Šimun Pekasa** fathering daughters there in **1719, 1734 and 1738**, the 1738 entry naming his wife **Mare** — against this archive's **Mara Pekass**, ahnentafel 427. **The sideways route this row proposed is the right one; it is the verdict «not on film» that was wrong.** See [notes/karlobag-is-indexed.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/karlobag-is-indexed.md).

rows.what: FindMyPast — a month's full subscription, and 386 people the archive stops following
rows.note:
**16 September 2026: a full month's subscription, where before there were three trial days.** That changes what is worth doing, because the trial's own closing note said what it could not do: *«Perković (2,036), Borić (2,007), Papić (1,042), Prpić (943), Boras (3,445) are too common to harvest in bulk. **They need a first name and a year.**»*

**`sources/findmypast/targets-2026-09-16.psv` is the first name and the year.** Generated from the archive rather than typed, so it cannot drift from the tree: **every published person born 1840–1910 with no death recorded** — old enough to sail, young enough to be on a post-1906 manifest. **386 people.** Žubrinić 115, Kalanj 95, Prpić 54, Blažević 50, Papić 25, Šestan 23, Perpić 12, Boras 7, Vukelić 4.

**It is not a list of emigrants. It is the list of people this archive stops following** — which is the same list until somebody looks. **Not one is a direct ancestor**, and that is worth saying plainly: this row buys breadth, not the line.

**Work it by surname, not by person.** One surname read end to end beats forty name searches, and the trial proved why: **`ZUBRINICH` returns 191 records and gives Australia; `ZUBRINIC` returns a different 119 and gives Lika** — Šumećica, Otočac, Prozor. Anyone searching one spelling is missing the other entirely. The file carries a **spellings** column with every variant this archive has met.

**The four things the trial left unfinished, and they come first:**

1. **Port Pirie electoral rolls — eight of nineteen unread.** This is the one already sitting in `searched.json` as **pending**. Rolls give an address and an occupation year by year. The archive records a trade for **16 people out of 1,245**; these could outweigh that several times over. In Lika this family held offices — forest warden, master of the watch, keeper of the prison. At Port Pirie they are labourers in a lead smelter, and [the trade page](/work/) says so on eight men. **The offices did not travel.**
2. **The remaining ~13 `zubrinic` manifests** — 106 of 119 were read. More Prozor and Šumećica residences, more named fathers.
3. **South Australian birth, marriage and death registrations** for the eighteen Australians. The one already done settled [a duplicate](/duplicates/): **one** 1886 Port Pirie registration, for a *Kate*, and no *Katalyn* in 176 records.
4. **Boras at Yarraville (1892) and Sydney (1919)** — never researched, and Boras is one of only two families that reaches Hedviga without scaffolding.

**Two negatives already paid for, so they are not re-tested.** FindMyPast holds **no Croatian parish registers** — so it cannot answer Brinje, and [row 50](/worklist/) still wants the film. And there is **nothing on Hedviga's 1948 emigration**: no *Hedviga Blazevic* anywhere, no Defranceski in *Passenger Lists Leaving UK 1890–1960*. **They went to South Africa and this service has neither end of the voyage.**

**Method, from the trial, worth a day on its own.** Only the pre-1925 Ellis manifests (`ELLIS2` transcripts) carry a **last residence and the relative left behind** — that residence is what turned the Kalanji from a Klenovica family into **Brinje** people. Ids ending `…/2` and `…/3` are **relations named on a record**, not passengers.

---

**Item 1 is done, 16 September 2026, the same day.** **All fifty** Australia Electoral Rolls transcripts for *Zubrinich* — nineteen people, five roll years, in `sources/findmypast/electoral-rolls-2026-09-16.psv` and written up in [notes/port-pirie-electoral-rolls.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/port-pirie-electoral-rolls.md). The `searched.json` row that had been **pending** since the trial expired is closed.

**The archive's occupation count went from 8 of these people to 23**, and `/work` gained a **fifth stratum** — *Port Pirie and Whyalla — the lead smelter* — which is now the **second-largest** after Senj. It should have existed already: this archive has been saying **«the offices did not travel»** while giving the destination nowhere to appear.

**Two trades and no third.** Foundry — *ironmoulder*, *moulder* — and *labourer*, plus one shop assistant. **Not one office, not one rank**, against *Silvarum Custos*, *Vigiliarum Magister*, *Custos Carcerum* and a municipal excise controller in Lika.

**And the rolls do what a register does.** Keith Leo and Rita Laurel move **9 Queen Street → 46 Cottell Street → 58 King Street** in four years. Two marriages fall between roll years — Asta Louise comes from an Adelaide suburb to Whyalla, Una Blanche from 11 Queen Street to 30 Beach Road. **Three separate Zubrinich households stand in Queen Street**, at 9, 11 and 65.

**One caution, proved inside this set: the «household members» field is not a household.** Maurice Joseph and Violet Mary share 56 Simpson Road in all three years and only the 1941 transcript lists them together. **Group by address, not by that field.**

**And the spelling lesson recurs one level down.** *Austa*/*Asta Louise*, *Benedicter*/*Benedieter*, *Valentino*/*Valentine*, *Una*/*Una Blanche* — **four of nineteen indexed twice inside a single record set**.

---

**Items 2 and 3 done the same day.**

**Item 2 — the manifests, and the spelling count. It was written here as «three and no more» and that was wrong within the hour.** Zubrinich **191**, Zubrinic **119**, **Zubrinick 10**, Zubrinec **1**; Subrinic, Xubrinich, Zubrinicz zero. **The first test was six guesses at how a CROATIAN ear would render the name. Zubrinick is how an AMERICAN CLERK did**, and no guessing from the Croatian side reaches it. **The spelling that finds a family is the one written by the person who could not spell it, in the country they arrived in.**

**The single `Zubrinec` record is the best thing on this list.** *Franc Zubrinec*, b.1887, *Adriatic* 1911, **residence «Sinae, Hungary»** — **SINAC**, on the Gacka near Otočac — father **Pavao**. **`parishes.psv` has carried Sinac since 14 September, with three films, and not one person in this tree has ever been placed there.** It has one now, and **Sinac births are filmed 1834–1901, so his 1887 baptism is inside the film.** He sailed on the same manifest page as **Anton Zubrinic of Prozor** — the record ids are three apart.

Also: **Eva Žubrinić of Prozor sailed from FIUME** on the *Ultonia* in 1907, where every other departure here is Southampton, Rotterdam or Liverpool. And **Gomerčić is a second family married in** after Kostelac — Eva met by a *brother-in-law* Joso Gomerčić, and Mijo Žubrinić recorded as *uncle* to the passenger Pavdo Gomerčić. **Neither family is in this tree.**

**Item 3 — the South Australian registers, and they carry the parents in the index row.** Thirty-five births, eleven marriages, fourteen deaths, no transcript needed. **John × Rose marry 1884 and have twelve children to 1909**; five of the six labouring men in the rolls are on that list and the sixth is a grandson. **The address guesses from the rolls are now on birth records** — Malcolm Theodore is Edward Malcolm's son, Gwenyth Florence is Arthur Leslie's daughter. **Michael Valentine lives alone in every roll because Minnie Doris died in 1932.**

**And they corrected me twice, within hours.** Thomas Leo and Una Blanche married in **1912** with nine children, not between the 1939 and 1941 rolls; Leonard Francis and Asta Louise at **Adelaide in 1936**, not between 1939 and 1943. Both slips came from reading the roll's «household members» field as a household — **the very trap the same note had already written down**, and it still caught me. Corrected in [notes/port-pirie-electoral-rolls.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/port-pirie-electoral-rolls.md).

**Item 4 is thin and the trial was right about it.** The archive's own Boras with no death are all at **Senj** — Christina Maria 1862, Franciscus Paul 1872, Marija 1892 and the rest. The Australian Boras are the English-named NSW family the trial dismissed. **Yarraville and Sydney are not reachable by a place filter** — FindMyPast's results URL does not take one — so this needs a name-and-year pass off the target list like any other common surname.

---

**PERPIĆ was tried, and it is a clean negative — which changes how the rest should be done.** `PRPIĆ` returns **943** and `PERPIĆ` **112**, the Zubrinich/Zubrinic split exactly, so it looked like the easy one. **Four Perpić passengers carry a residence and they are four different places** — *Kastav*, *Matkovići*, *Karlovac*, *Zeria* — **not one of them Krivi Put or Senj**, and no two near each other. The other hundred are an American family at **Perry, Wyoming County, New York**, with a later limb at San Diego and Bergen County.

**That is the Kalanj lesson again, and it should now be a rule**: the trial wrote *«Kalanj is a regional surname, not one household»*, and **Perpić is the same**. **A Croatian surname on a US manifest index is a region, not a family.** Harvesting one in bulk buys nothing without a place to test it against — so **Šestan 519, Papić 1,042, Blažević 1,374 and Vukelić 2,424 should not be swept at all.** They should be worked **name and year at a time off the 386**, which is what that list was built for.

**The sweep gave two things anyway.** Joka Perpić's 1911 record spells **the daughter PERPIC and her father PRPIC in the same entry** — the two spellings shown to be one surname by the index's own hand. And she sailed **from FIUME**, the second Fiume departure in this material after Eva Žubrinić in 1907. **Fiume is a route this evidence keeps showing**, and it is three hours from Senj rather than a crossing of Europe.

---

**And the obvious escape from that rule was tested and does not exist.** If a surname returns a region, then search the **village** instead — FindMyPast's results URL takes `keywords=`, and the form calls it *«Optional keywords»*.

**It looked like it worked**: `keywords=smokvica` returns **13** passenger records. They are Banićević, Gabrijel, Pešelj, Radovanović, Šalečić, Šeparović, Teodorović, Tomašić — and the first transcript reads **«Residence: Smokvica, DALMATIA»**. That is the **Smokvica on Korčula**, four hundred kilometres from Smokvica Krmpotska. **A village name is no more unique than a surname.**

**Then every one of this archive's villages returned nothing** — *krmpot*, *krivi put*, *sumecica*, *klenovica*, *jablanac*, *sinac*, *prozor*, all **0** — **including the misspellings the records themselves use**: *prozov* 0, *otochetz* 0, *sumenica* 0.

**The decisive test.** Eva Žubrinić's 1907 record gives *Residence: **Prozor*** and *Ship: **Ultonia***. `lastname=zubrinic&keywords=prozor` → **0**. `&keywords=ultonia` → **0**. **Her own record is not returned by her own village or her own ship.** The residence is on the transcript and **not in the index**: readable once you have found someone, useless for finding them.

**So there is no way in by place, and a common surname returns a region. The only handle is a name with a year beside it.** `targets-2026-09-16.psv` was built as a convenience. It turns out to be **the only instrument there is**, and the rest of the month should be spent working down it.

---

**The instrument was here all along: the NATURALISATION PETITION.**

A manifest gives a residence and a relative. **A petition gives an exact birth date, an exact birth place, the spouse's birth date and every child's birth date — a whole household in one row.** Ivan Žubrinić's also carries the alias **«Or Rozić»** — which a first reading took for his wife's maiden name and **is not**: the index attaches it to **Ivan and all three children** too. It is an alternate surname for the whole household, and reading it as a maiden name would have invented a marriage line that is not there.

**And in this set the birthplace IS indexed**, where in the passenger lists it is not: `keywords=otocac` **7**, `keywords=senj` **12** — against **0** for *prozor* in both. **The village search works after all: on towns, in the petitions only.** That is the seam the rest of the month should be worked in, and it is a better one than the 386.

**Two Senj-born emigrants in this archive's own surnames, neither of them recorded here.** **Marijan Vukelić**, b.1894, born **Senj**, five filings **1935–1948** (also indexed *Vjkelic*) — the line Milka Papić married into. And **Miro Šojat** (*Sojath*), b.1910, born **Senj**, 1955.

**A trap that nearly put a false negative in the archive.** Four surname-and-dataset searches came back **0** — Blažević, Prpić, Papić, Šestan in the passenger lists — and *«no Blažević emigration records exist»* was one keystroke from being written down. **They were not zero.** The check polled for the word *«results»*, which appears in the filter panel as *«View N results»* **before the count renders**. Polling for **a digit followed by «results»** gives **Blažević 706, Prpić 632, Papić 529**. **A negative is a finding and has to be earned like one.** The corrected Blažević probes are honest negatives: *Mile* → **Dvor**, *Joso* → **Kuthuryevac**, *Jurko* → nothing.

---

**Four petitions read out, and the seam is Otočac and Senj.** `keywords=` gives **Otočac 7** and **Senj 12**; **Karlobag 0**, **Novi Vinodolski 0**. **The match is fuzzy** — searching *klada* returns a page largely of **Greek** names — so **a hit is a candidate and the transcript is the test**. All four below were opened and read.
